title: حِكَايَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ
titleEn: The Tailor's Tale, continued: the Barber's Brothers — the Butcher's Brother, the Glass-Seller, the Cropped-Eared Beggar and the Cut-Lipped Man; the Tale's End
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 266–276 (Night 33, continuing directly from nights-32), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 33 completes the barber's account of his brothers to the Caliph. The fifth brother's daydream ends in smashed glass; a woman's gift of gold draws him into a procuress's trap, where a black slave salts his wounds, but he returns in disguise, kills the slave and the old woman, plunders the house and is banished by the governor, then mutilated by robbers. The sixth, cut-lipped brother is fed an imaginary banquet by a jesting Barmakid, whom he slaps in kind and who makes him his boon companion; he is later mutilated again by a Bedouin. The barber then defends himself, the Caliph exiles him, and the tailor ends his tale before the king of China; the king, preferring it to the hunchback's story, sends for the barber. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some of the Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّٰلِثَةُ وَالثَّلَٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when the night, the third and the thirty, came to be,
sentences.i: When the thirty-third night came,
sentences.n: The edition prints the ordinal as الثلثة (the long ā of ثالثة is not written) and the tens in the nominative plural, الثلثون; both are vocalised as they stand, the missing ā with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ أَخَ الْمُزَيِّنِ قَالَ ثُمَّ أَطْرَقَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna akha al-muzayyini qāla thumma aṭraqa ilā al-arḍi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that the brother of the barber said — then he bowed (his head) to the ground —
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the barber's brother said — and then he bowed his head toward the ground —
sentences.n: The speaker is Shahrazād. The barber is telling the caliph about one of his brothers, who goes on to speak in the first person. أخ is printed without the alif of the accusative (أخًا); it is vocalised with a plain fatḥa.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَزَلْ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ جِلَاؤُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lam azal kadhālika ḥattā yatimma jilāʾuhā
sentences.l: and I did not cease (to be) thus until her unveiling is completed
sentences.i: and I will stay so until the display of her is complete
sentences.n: From here to the end of the daydream the brother is picturing the wedding he will make; the print mixes past and present forms, and the translation follows the dream as future. جِلَاء is the 'unveiling' (jalwa) of the bride, when she is shown to her husband.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي آ أَمُرُ بَعْضَ الْخَدَمِ أَنْ يَرْمِيَ كِيسًا فِيهِ خَمْسَمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innī ā amuru baʿḍa al-khadami an yarmiya kīsan fīhi khamsamiʾati dīnārin
sentences.l: then indeed I — ā (stray) — I command some of the servants that he throw a purse, in it five-hundred of dinars,
sentences.i: Then I will order one of the servants to cast down a purse with five hundred dinars in it,
sentences.n: The lone آ before امر is a doubling in the print (the verb is أَمُرُ / آمُرُ 'I command'); it is left standing as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تُحْضَرَا دَفَعَهُ لِلْمَوَاشِطِ وَآمُرُهُمْ أَنْ يُدْخِلُونِي عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā tuḥḍarā dafaʿahu li-al-mawāshiṭi wa-āmuruhum an yudkhilūnī ʿalayhā
sentences.l: and when she is brought, he gave it to the hairdressers, and I command them that they bring me in to her
sentences.i: and when the bride is brought, he hands it to the hairdressers, and I order them to bring me in to her.
sentences.n: تحضرا ends in a stray alif; I take it as 'she is brought' (passive), with the servant as the subject of دفعه. The reading is uncertain. The مواشط are the women who dress and adorn the bride.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا دَخَلُوا بِهَا فَلَا أَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا وَلَا أُكَلِّمُهَـــا احْتِقَارًالِأَنْ يُقَالَ إِنِّي عَزِيزُ النَّفْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā dakhalū bihā fa-lā anẓuru ilayhā wa-lā ukallimuhā iḥtiqāran li-an yuqāla innī ʿazīzu al-nafsi
sentences.l: And when they enter with her, I do not look at her and I do not speak to her — contempt, so that it be said: I am dear-of-self.
sentences.i: When they lead her in, I will neither look at her nor speak to her, in disdain, so that it will be said, 'He is a man of proud spirit.'
sentences.n: احتقارالان is printed run together and is read as two words, احتقارًا لأن 'in contempt, so that'. عزيز النفس, 'dear of self', means self-respecting, hard to please, proud.

sentences.t: وَتَجِيئُ أُمُّهَا فَتُقَبِّلُ رَأْسِى وَيَدَيَّ وَتَقُولُ لِي يَاسَيِّدِي
sentences.tr: wa-tajīʾu ummuhā fa-tuqabbilu raʾsī wa-yadayya wa-taqūlu lī yā sayyidī
sentences.l: And her mother comes, and kisses my head and my two hands, and says to me: O my lord,
sentences.i: Then her mother comes and kisses my head and my hands, and says to me, 'O my lord,'
sentences.n: راسى is printed with a final ى (unpointed) for ي; ويدي is read as the dual, 'my two hands'.

sentences.t: انْظُرْ جَارِيَتَكَ فَإِنَّهَا تَشْتَهِى قُرْبَكَ فَاجْبُرْ بِخَاطِرِهَا فَلَا أَرُدُّ عَلَيْهَا جَوَابًا
sentences.tr: unẓur jāriyataka fa-innahā tashtahī qurbaka fa-ajbur bi-khāṭirihā fa-lā aruddu ʿalayhā jawāban
sentences.l: Look at your slave-girl, for she desires your nearness; so mend (things) with her heart! — and I do not return to her an answer.
sentences.i: 'Look upon your handmaid, for she longs for your nearness; comfort her heart.' But I give her no answer.
sentences.n: جبر بخاطره is a set phrase, 'to soothe someone's feelings'; the verb chooses the بِـ. The mother's speech ends at بخاطرها.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا رَأَتْ ذَلِكَ مِنِّى قَامَتْ وَبَاسَتْ رِجْلَيَّ مِرَارًا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā raʾat dhālika minnī qāmat wa-bāsat rijlayya mirāran
sentences.l: And when she sees that from me, she rises and kisses my two feet repeatedly,
sentences.i: When she sees this in me, she rises and kisses my feet again and again,

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقُـولُ يَاسَيِّدِي إِنَّ بِنْتِي صَبِيَّةٌ مَلِيحَةٌ مَارَأَتْ رَجُلًا
sentences.tr: thumma taqūlu yā sayyidī inna bintī ṣabiyyatun malīḥatun mā raʾat rajulan
sentences.l: then says: O my lord, indeed my daughter is a girl, a pretty one; she has not seen a man.
sentences.i: and then says, 'My lord, my daughter is a pretty young girl who has never seen a man.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا رَأَتْ مِنْكَ هَذَا الِانْقِبَــاضَ انْكَسَرَ خَاطِرُهَا فَمِلْ إِلَيْهَا وَكَلِّمْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā raʾat minka hādhā al-inqibāḍa inkasara khāṭiruhā fa-mil ilayhā wa-kallimhā
sentences.l: So if she sees from you this withdrawal, her heart is broken; so incline to her and speak to her.
sentences.i: If she sees such coldness in you, her heart will break. Turn to her and speak with her.'
sentences.n: انقباض, 'contraction', is here the reserved, withdrawn manner of the bridegroom.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا تَقُومُ وَتُحْضِرُلِي قَدَحًا فِيهِ شَرَابٌ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā taqūmu wa-tuḥḍirulī qadaḥan fīhi sharābun
sentences.l: Then indeed she rises and brings me a cup, in it a drink,
sentences.i: Then she rises and brings me a cup with a drink in it,
sentences.n: تحضرلي is printed as one word; read tuḥḍiru lī.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ بِنْتَهَا تَأْخُذُ الْقَدَحَ فَإِذَا جَاءَتْنِى تَرَكْتُهَا قَائِمَةً بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ
sentences.tr: thumma inna bintahā taʾkhudhu al-qadaḥa fa-idhā jāʾatnī taraktuhā qāʾimatan bayna yadayya
sentences.l: Then indeed her daughter takes the cup, and when she comes to me, I leave her standing between my two hands,
sentences.i: Then her daughter takes the cup, and when she comes to me I leave her standing before me,

sentences.t: وَأَنَا عَلَى مُدَوَّرَةٍ مُزَرْكَشٍ مُتَّكِىً لَا أَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا مِنْ كِبْرِ نَفْسِي حَتَّى تَقُولَ لِي إِنِّي سُلْطَانٌ عَظِيمُ الشَّأْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā ʿalā mudawwaratin muzarkashin muttakiʾan lā anẓuru ilayhā min kibri nafsī ḥattā taqūla lī innī sulṭānun ʿaẓīmu al-shaʾni
sentences.l: while I am upon a round (cushion), embroidered, reclining; I do not look at her, from the pride of my self, until she says to me that I am a sultan, great of rank.
sentences.i: while I recline on an embroidered round cushion, not looking at her, so great is my pride, until she tells me that I am a sultan of lofty station.
sentences.n: مدورة (the round seat or cushion) is feminine, but the adjective مزركش 'embroidered' is printed masculine, a Middle Arabic lapse in agreement. متكىً is printed with the tanwīn mark and no hamza; it reads muttakiʾan, 'reclining'. The clause حتى تقول لي is awkward; the sense seems to be 'until she is moved to say that I am a mighty sultan'.

sentences.t: فَتَقُولُ لِي يَا سَيِّدِي بِحَقِّ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ لَا تَرُدَّ الْقَدَحَ مِنْ يَدِ جَارِيَتِكَ فَإِنِّي جَارِيَتُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-taqūlu lī yā sayyidī bi-ḥaqqi Allāhi ʿalayka lā tarudda al-qadaḥa min yadi jāriyatika fa-innī jāriyatuka
sentences.l: And she says to me: O my lord, by the right of God upon you, do not reject the cup from the hand of your slave-girl, for I am your slave-girl.
sentences.i: Then she says to me, 'My lord, by the claim God has upon you, do not refuse the cup from your handmaid's hand, for I am your handmaid.

sentences.t: فَلَا أُكَلِّمُهَا فَتُلِحُّ عَلَيَّ وَتَقُولُ لَابُدَّ مِنْ شُرْبِهِ وَ تُقَدِّمُهُ إِلَي فَمِي
sentences.tr: fa-lā ukallimuhā fa-tulliḥḥu ʿalayya wa-taqūlu lā budda min shurbihi wa-taqdimuhu ilā famī
sentences.l: And I do not speak to her, so she insists upon me and says: there is no escaping the drinking of it — and she brings it forward to my mouth.
sentences.i: I do not speak to her, so she presses me and says, 'You must drink it,' and holds it up to my mouth.'
sentences.n: The edition prints a space after the و of وتقدمه; it is kept as a separate token.

sentences.t: فَأَنْفُضُ يَلْرِي فِي وَجْهِهَا وَأَرْفُسُهَا بِرِجْلِي
sentences.tr: fa-anfuḍu yalrī fī wajhihā wa-arfusuhā bi-rijlī
sentences.l: then I shake yalrī [unclear] in her face and I kick her with my foot
sentences.i: then I shake my hand(?) in her face and kick her with my foot
sentences.n: يلري is not a word. Most likely it is a misprint for يدي 'my hands' (ل for د, ر for ي), and the sense would be 'I flick my hands in her face'; it is vocalised here as printed, as a form that cannot be explained.

sentences.t: وَأَعْمَلُ هَكَذَا ثُمَّ رَفَسَ بِرِجْلِهِ فَوَقَعَ الزُّجَاجُ وَالْقَفَصُ وَكَانَ فِي مَكَانٍ مُرْتَفِعٍ فَنَزَلَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ فَتَكَسَّرَ كُلُّ مَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿmalu hākadhā thumma rafasa bi-rijlihi fa-waqaʿa al-zujāju wa-al-qafaṣu wa-kāna fī makānin murtafiʿin fa-nazala ilā al-arḍi fa-takassara kullu mā fīhi
sentences.l: and I do thus — then he kicked with his foot, and the glass fell, and the crate, and it was in a high place, and it came down to the ground, and everything in it was shattered.
sentences.i: 'And I do just so!' — and with that he kicked out with his foot, and the glassware fell, and the crate with it, which stood in a high place; it came down to the ground, and everything in it was smashed.
sentences.n: The narrator moves from the dream (present tense, 'I') to what actually happened ('he kicked'). The القفص is the wicker crate or tray that held his glass.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَ أَخِي وَقَالَ هَذَا كُلُّهُ مِنْ كِبْرِ نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥa akhī wa-qāla hādhā kulluhu min kibri nafsī
sentences.l: Then my brother cried out and said: All this is from the pride of my self.
sentences.i: My brother cried out and said, 'All this comes of my pride!'

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَطَمَ أَخِي عَلَى وَجْهِهِ وَخَرَقَ ثِيَابَهُ وَجَعَلَ يَبْكِي وَيَلْطِمُ وَالنَّاسُ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ رَائِحُونَ إِلَى صَلَوةِ الْجُمُعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika yā amīra al-muʾminīna laṭama akhī ʿalā wajhihi wa-kharaqa thiyābahu wa-jaʿala yabkī wa-yalṭimu wa-al-nāsu yanẓurūna ilayhi wa-hum rāʾiḥūna ilā ṣalāti al-jumuʿati
sentences.l: So at that, O commander of the believers, my brother struck upon his face, and tore his garments, and began to weep and to strike, while the people were looking at him, and they were going to the prayer of the Friday.
sentences.i: At that, O Commander of the Faithful, my brother struck his face, tore his clothes, and began to weep and beat himself, while the people looked on, on their way to the Friday prayer.
sentences.n: Here the barber speaks again, addressing the caliph. أميرالمؤمنين is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ نَظَرَهُ وَرَحِمَهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ لَمْ يُفَكِّرْ فِيهِ وَأَخِي عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ رَاحَ مِنْهُ الْمَالُ وَالرِّبْحُ
sentences.tr: fa-minhum man naẓarahu wa-raḥimahu wa-minhum man lam yufakkir fīhi wa-akhī ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati rāḥa minhu al-mālu wa-al-ribḥu
sentences.l: and among them (were) those who looked at him and pitied him, and among them (were) those who did not give thought to him; and my brother, in that state — gone from him were the money and the profit.
sentences.i: Some of them looked at him and pitied him, and some gave him no thought; and my brother, in that plight, had lost both his capital and his profit.
sentences.n: نظره is used as a transitive verb, 'looked at him'; Classical Arabic would say نظر إليه. In Middle Arabic, verbs of this kind often govern the object directly.

sentences.t: فَأَقَامَ سَاعَةً يَبْكِي
sentences.tr: fa-aqāma sāʿatan yabkī
sentences.l: So he remained an hour, weeping,
sentences.i: He stayed there an hour, weeping,

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِا مْرَأَةٍ حَسَنَةٍ وَمَعَهَا عِدَّةُ خُدَّامٍ وَهِيَ رَاكِبَةٌ عَلَى بَغْلَةٍ بِسَرْجِ ذَهَبٍ يَفُوحُ الْمِسْكُ مِنْهَا وَهِيَ مَاشِيَةٌ إِلَى صَلَوةِ الْجُمُعَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-imraʾatin ḥasanatin wa-maʿahā ʿiddatu khuddāmin wa-hiya rākibatun ʿalā baghlatin bi-sarji dhahabin yafūḥu al-misku minhā wa-hiya māshiyatun ilā ṣalāti al-jumuʿati
sentences.l: and behold, with a woman, beautiful, and with her a number of servants, and she riding upon a mule with a saddle of gold, musk wafting from her, and she going to the prayer of the Friday.
sentences.i: when suddenly there came a beautiful woman with a number of attendants, riding a mule with a golden saddle, the scent of musk wafting from her, on her way to the Friday prayer.
sentences.n: با مراة is printed split in two, for بامرأة; the بِـ after وإذا only marks what appears. ماشية 'walking' sits oddly beside راكبة 'riding'; read it loosely as 'going, proceeding'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتْ إِلَى الزُّجَاجَاتِ وَحَالِ أَخِي وَبُكَائِهِ أَخَذَ هَا الْحُزْنُ عَلَيْهِ وَرَقَّ قَلْبُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarat ilā al-zujājāti wa-ḥāli akhī wa-bukāʾihi akhadha hā al-ḥuznu ʿalayhi wa-raqqa qalbuhā
sentences.l: And when she looked at the glass pieces and the state of my brother and his weeping, sorrow for him took her, and her heart grew tender,
sentences.i: When she saw the glassware and my brother's state and his weeping, sorrow for him seized her and her heart softened,
sentences.n: اخذ ها is printed with a space before the pronoun; read akhadhahā.

sentences.t: وَسَأَلَتْ عَنْ حَالِهِ فَقِيلَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَعَهُ طَبَقُ زُجَاجٍ يَتَعَيَّشُ مِنْهُ فَانْكَسَرَ مِنْهُ فَأَصَابَهُ مَاتَرَيْنَ
sentences.tr: wa-saʾalat ʿan ḥālihi fa-qīla innahu kāna maʿahu ṭabaqu zujājin yataʿayyashu minhu fa-inkasara minhu fa-aṣābahu mā tarayna
sentences.l: and she asked about his state, and it was said: indeed he had with him a tray of glass from which he made his living, and it broke from him, and there befell him what you see.
sentences.i: and she asked about him, and was told, 'He had a tray of glassware from which he made his living; it broke, and what you see has befallen him.'
sentences.n: ماترين is printed as one word, 'what you (f.) see'.

sentences.t: فَنَادَتْ بَعْضَ الْخُدَّامِ وَقَٰلَتْ لَهُ ادْفَعْ الَّذِي مَعَكَ لِهَذَا الْمِسْكِينِ فَدَفَعَ لَهُ صُرَّةً وَجَدَ فِيهَا خَمْسَمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-nādat baʿḍa al-khuddāmi wa-qālat lahu idfaʿ alladhī maʿaka li-hādhā al-miskīni fa-dafaʿa lahu ṣurratan wajada fīhā khamsamiʾati dīnārin
sentences.l: and she called one of the servants and said to him: give what is with you to this poor one; and he gave him a purse, he found in it five-hundred of dinars.
sentences.i: She called one of her servants and said to him, 'Give what you have with you to this poor man.' He gave him a purse, and in it he found five hundred dinars.
sentences.n: وقلت is printed for وقالت (a defective spelling; it is pointed with the dagger alif so that it reads qālat). The final clause 'he found in it' is the brother, who opens the purse.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَقَعَتْ فِي يَدِهِ كَادَ أَنْ يَمُوتَ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْفَرَحِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waqaʿat fī yadihi kāda an yamūta min shiddati al-faraḥi
sentences.l: and when it fell into his hand, he almost died from the intensity of the joy,
sentences.i: and when it fell into his hand he nearly died of sheer joy,
sentences.n: كاد أن يموت: with كاد the verb normally stands without أن; here أن is added, as is common in later Arabic.

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ أَخِي بِالدُّعَاءِ لَهَا وَعَادَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ غَنِيًّا وَقَعَدَ مُتَفَكِّرًا وَإِذَا بِالْبَابِ يَدُقُّ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala akhī bi-al-duʿāʾi lahā wa-ʿāda ilā manzilihi ghaniyyan wa-qaʿada mutafakkiran wa-idhā bi-al-bābi yaduqqu
sentences.l: and my brother turned to praying for her, and returned to his house rich, and sat thinking; and behold, at the door, one knocks —
sentences.i: My brother turned to praying for her, and went back to his house a rich man, and sat there deep in thought, when behold, someone was knocking at the door.
sentences.n: يدق has no stated subject: 'one knocks'. The بِـ after وإذا marks what appears, here the knocking at the door.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَفَتَحَ وَإِذَا بِعَجُوزٍ لَا يَعْرِفُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-fataḥa wa-idhā bi-ʿajūzin lā yaʿrifuhā
sentences.l: and he rose and opened, and behold, an old woman whom he did not know,
sentences.i: He rose and opened it, and there stood an old woman he did not know,

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي اعْلَمْ أَنَّ الصَّلَوةَ قَدْ قَرُبَتْ وَأَنَا بِغَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ وَأُحِبُّ أَنْ تُوَسِّعَ لِي مَنْزِلَكَ حَتَّى أَتَوَضَّأَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu yā waladī iʿlam anna al-ṣalāta qad qarubat wa-anā bi-ghayri wuḍūʾin wa-uḥibbu an tuwassiʿa lī manzilaka ḥattā atawaḍḍaʾa
sentences.l: and she said to him: O my son, know that the prayer has drawn near, and I am without ablution, and I like that you make-spacious for me your house until I perform ablution.
sentences.i: who said to him, 'My son, know that the hour of prayer has drawn near, and I am without ablution. I would like you to make room for me in your house, so that I may perform my ablutions.'
sentences.n: The old woman is the bawd of the story, as the reader will soon see. وضوء is the ritual washing before prayer.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: and he said: hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: He answered, 'With hearing and obedience.'
sentences.n: An accusative of reply (the verb is understood): 'I give you hearing and obedience', a courteous formula for 'gladly'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ أَخِي وَأَمَرَهَا بِالدُّخُولِ فَدَخَلَتْ وَدَفَعَ لَهَا إِبْرِيقًا تَتَوَضَّأَبِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala akhī wa-amarahā bi-al-dukhūli fa-dakhalat wa-dafaʿa lahā ibrīqan tatawaḍḍaʾa bihi
sentences.l: Then my brother entered and commanded her to enter, and she entered, and he gave her a ewer, she perform-ablution with it,
sentences.i: Then my brother went in and told her to enter, and she came in, and he gave her a ewer with which to perform her ablutions,
sentences.n: تتوضأبه is printed as one word, tatawaḍḍaʾa bihi, 'that she perform ablution with it'; the subjunctive has no stated particle.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَ أَخِي وَهُوَ طَائِرٌ مِنَ الْفَرَحِ بِالدَّنَانِيرِ ثُمَّ صَرَّهَا فِي الْهِمْيَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasa akhī wa-huwa ṭāʾirun mina al-faraḥi bi-al-danānīri thumma ṣarrahā fī al-himyāni
sentences.l: and my brother sat, and he flying from the joy in the dinars; then he tied them up in the money-belt.
sentences.i: My brother sat down, fairly flying with joy over the dinars, and tied them up in his money-belt.
sentences.n: طائر من الفرح, 'flying with joy', is an idiom for being beside oneself with delight.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ هَذَا وَفَرَغَتِ الْعَجُوزُ مِنَ الْوُضُوءِ أَقْبَلَتْ إِلَى الْمَوْضِعِ الَّذِي هُوَ جَالِسٌ فِيهِ أَخِي وَصَلَّتْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min hādhā wa-faraghati al-ʿajūzu mina al-wuḍūʾi aqbalat ilā al-mawḍiʿi alladhī huwa jālisun fīhi akhī wa-ṣallat rakʿatayni
sentences.l: And when he finished with this and the old woman finished with the ablution, she came to the place which he was sitting in, my brother, and prayed two bowings.
sentences.i: When he had finished with this, and the old woman with her ablutions, she came to the place where my brother was sitting, and prayed two rakʿas.
sentences.n: In 'the place which he sits in, my brother' the name is added after the pronoun for clarity, a looseness of word order common in this text. A رَكْعَة is one cycle of bowing and prostration in prayer.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَعَتْ لِأَخِي دُعَاءً حَسَنًا فَشَكَرَهَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَمَدَّيَدَهُ إِلَى الدَّنَانِيرِ وَدَفَعَ لَهَا دِينَارَيْنِ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ هَذِهِ صَدَقَةٌ عَنِّي
sentences.tr: thumma daʿat li-akhī duʿāʾan ḥasanan fa-shakarahā ʿalā dhālika wa-madda yadahu ilā al-danānīri wa-dafaʿa lahā dīnārayni wa-qāla fī nafsihi hādhihi ṣadaqatun ʿannī
sentences.l: Then she prayed for my brother a good prayer, and he thanked her for that, and stretched out his hand to the dinars, and gave her two dinars, and said within himself: this is alms on my behalf.
sentences.i: Then she prayed a fair prayer for my brother, and he thanked her for it, and put his hand to the dinars and gave her two of them, saying to himself, 'This is alms given for my sake.'
sentences.n: ومديده is printed as one word, wa-madda yadahu.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتِ الدَّنَانِيرَ قَالَتْ يَا سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ لِمَ نَظَرْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ حُبِّكَ بَسْمَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾati al-danānīra qālat yā subḥāna Allāhi li-ma naẓarta ilayya min ḥubbika basmatan
sentences.l: And when she saw the dinars, she said: O glory-of God, why did you look at me, from your love, a smile?
sentences.i: But when she saw the dinars she said, 'Glory be to God! Why have you looked at me...'
sentences.n: The sentence continues in the next unit. The last words (من حبك بسمة) are obscure to me; they are vocalised provisionally, and the translation is a rough guess to be settled by what follows.

sentences.t: الصُّعَالِيكِ خُذْ مَا لَكَ مِنِّي بِهِ حَاجَةٌ وَارْدُدْهُ إِلَى قَلْبِكَ
sentences.tr: al-ṣaʿālīki khudh mā laka minnī bihi ḥājatun wa-ardudhu ilā qalbika
sentences.l: …the vagabonds. Take what (is) to-you; from-me, in-it (is) a need; and return-it to your heart.
sentences.i: …the paupers. Take back what is yours; I have no need of it. Set your heart at ease.
sentences.n: The sentence begins before this unit: الصعاليك closes a clause spoken by the old woman. مني به حاجة reads literally ‘from me, in it, a need’; the sense wanted is ‘I have no need of it’, so a negative has dropped out, or ما لي به حاجة is meant — the print is unclear. واردده إلى قلبك, literally ‘return it to your heart’, I take as ‘take heart, be reassured’; this is a best guess.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تُرِيدُ الاِجْتِمَاعَ مِنَ الَّذِي أَعْطَتْكَ الْمَالَ اجْتَمَعَ لَكَ مَعَهَا وَهِيَ صَاحِبَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-in kunta turīdu al-ijtimāʿa min al-ladhī aʿṭatka al-māla ijtamaʿa laka maʿahā wa-hiya ṣāḥibatī
sentences.l: So if you were wanting the meeting-together with the-one-who gave-you the wealth, there-was-a-meeting for-you with-her; and she (is) my mistress.
sentences.i: If it is union with her who gave you the money that you desire, then you shall have it, for she is my own mistress.
sentences.n: الذي is the masculine relative standing for the woman (Classical الَّتِي): a Middle Arabic levelling. The apodosis is a bare perfect, اجتمع لك, ‘it has come about for you’ — a promise put as accomplished.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي يَا أُمِّي كَيْفَ الْحِيلَةُ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī yā ummī kayfa al-ḥīlatu ilayhā
sentences.l: So said my-brother: “O my-mother, how (is) the contrivance to-her?”
sentences.i: My brother said, “Mother, how is she to be won?”
sentences.n: الحيلة إليها, ‘the device unto her’, is ‘the means of getting to her’. The narrator, the Barber, passes here from his own voice to the old woman’s, and back again in the next sentence; the print gives no sign of it.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ يَا وَلَدِي إِنَّهَا تَمِيلُ إِلَى رَجُلٍ مُوسِرٍ فَخُذْ جَمِيعَ مَالِكَ مَعَكَ وَاتَّبِعْنِي لِأَ دُلَّكَ عَلَى الْمُرَادِ
sentences.tr: qultu yā waladī innahā tamīlu ilā rajulin mūsirin fa-khudh jamīʿa mālika maʿaka wa-ittabiʿnī li-a dullaka ʿalā al-murādi
sentences.l: I said: “O my-son, she inclines to a man, well-off; so take all your-wealth with you and follow-me, that I-may-guide-you to the desired.”
sentences.i: I said, “My son, she is drawn to a man of means. Take all your money with you and follow me, and I shall lead you to what you desire.”
sentences.n: Now the old woman speaks in the first person (قلت), still as the Barber relays it. لا دلك is printed as two words; it is لِأَدُلَّكَ ‘so that I may guide you’ with a stray space, kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا اجْتَمَعْتَ بِهَا فَلَا تُخْلِي شَيْأً مِنَ الْمُلَاطَفَةِ وَالْكَلَامِ الْحَسَنِ إِلَّا وَتَفْعَلُهُ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā ijtamaʿta bihā fa-lā tukhlī shayʾan min al-mulāṭafati wa-al-kalāmi al-ḥasani illā wa-tafʿaluhu maʿahā
sentences.l: So when you have-met with-her, then do-not leave-empty anything of the gentle-dealing and the speech, the fair, except (that) you-do-it with-her.
sentences.i: And when you are with her, let no tenderness and no fair word go unspent, but do all of it for her.
sentences.n: تخلي is the indicative form where Classical wants the jussive تُخْلِ after لا: the final -ī is kept. إلا و… (‘except that…’) is a common idiom meaning ‘without doing it’.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّكَ تَنَالُ مِنْ جَمَالِهَا وَمِنْ مَا لِهَا جَمِيعَ مَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-innaka tanālu min jamālihā wa-min mā lihā jamīʿa mā turīdu
sentences.l: For indeed-you will-obtain, from her beauty and from her wealth, all that you-want.
sentences.i: For then you will win from her beauty and her wealth everything you could wish.
sentences.n: ما لها is printed as two words, but it is مالها ‘her wealth’; I keep the print’s spacing and vocalise the two halves to read as one.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ أَخِي جَمِيعَ الذَّهَبِ وَقَامَ وَمَشَى مَعَهَا وَهُوَلَا يُصَدِّقُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha akhī jamīʿa al-dhahabi wa-qāma wa-mashā maʿahā wa-huwa lā yuṣaddiqu
sentences.l: So took my-brother all the gold, and rose, and walked with-her, and he (was) not believing.
sentences.i: So my brother took all his gold, rose, and walked off with her, scarcely believing his luck.
sentences.n: وهولا is printed as a single word, وهو لا ‘and he not…’. يصدق without an object is ‘he could not believe it (his good fortune)’.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ تَزَلْ هِيَ تَمْشِي وَأَخِي تَابِعُهَا إِلَى بَابٍ كَبِيرٍ فَدَقَّتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam tazal hiya tamshī wa-akhī tābiʿuhā ilā bābin kabīrin fa-daqqathu
sentences.l: And she did-not cease, she, walking, and my-brother her-follower, to a door, big; and she-knocked-it.
sentences.i: On she walked, with my brother following after her, until they came to a great door, and she knocked at it.
sentences.n: تابعها is a participle with a pronoun, ‘her follower’, here a circumstantial clause (‘my brother following her’).

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتْ جَارِيَةٌ رُومِيَّةٌ فَفَتَحَتِ الْبَابَ فَدَخَلَتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَأَمَرَتْ أَخِي بِالدُّخُولِ مَعَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-kharajat jāriyatun rūmiyyatun fa-fataḥati al-bāba fa-dakhalati al-ʿajūzu wa-amarat akhī bi-al-dukhūli maʿahā
sentences.l: Then came-out a girl, a Roman-one; and she-opened the door, and entered the old-woman, and commanded my-brother with-the-entering with-her.
sentences.i: Out came a Greek slave-girl, who opened the door; the old woman went in and bade my brother enter with her.
sentences.n: رومية means from Rūm, the Byzantine or Greek lands, so a Greek or European slave-girl.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ إِلَى دَارٍ كَبِيرَةٍ وَمَجْلِسٍ كَبِيرٍ مَفْرُوشٍ أَرْضُهُ بِالزَّوَالِى الْعَجِيبَةِ وَسُتُورٍ مُعَلَّقَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ilā dārin kabīratin wa-majlisin kabīrin mafrūshin arḍuhu bi-al-zawālī al-ʿajībati wa-sutūrin muʿallaqatin
sentences.l: So he-entered into a house, big, and a sitting-room, big, spread (as to) its-floor with-the-carpets, the wondrous, and curtains, hung.
sentences.i: He passed into a spacious house and a great hall whose floor was spread with wondrous carpets, and hung with curtains.
sentences.n: الزوالي is the plural of زُولِيَّة / زِلِّيَّة, a rug or carpet; this is my best reading of an unusual word. I read وستور معلقة as a further item in the room (‘and curtains hung’), though the grammar could also join it to the carpets.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَ أَخِي وَوَضَعَ الذَّهَبَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَوَضَعَ عِمَامَتَهُ عَلَى رُكْبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-jalasa akhī wa-waḍaʿa al-dhahaba bayna yadayhi wa-waḍaʿa ʿimāmatahu ʿalā rukbatihi
sentences.l: So sat my-brother, and put the gold between his-two-hands, and put his-turban upon his-knee.
sentences.i: My brother sat down and set the gold before him, and laid his turban on his knee.
sentences.n: بين يديه, ‘between his two hands’, is the ordinary ‘in front of him’.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَجَارِيَةٌ أَقْبَلَتْ مَارَأَتِ الرَّاؤُنَ أَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lam yashʿur illā wa-jāriyatun aqbalat mā raʾati al-rāʾuna aḥsana minhā
sentences.l: And he-did-not perceive, except and a girl had-come-forward — (than whom) not saw the-seers (any) fairer than her.
sentences.i: Before he knew it a girl came in, lovelier than eye ever saw.
sentences.n: مارات is one word in the print: ما رأت, ‘(that) have not seen’. Its verb is feminine singular though its subject الراؤن is a masculine plural, and the plural is spelled without the usual wāw (الراؤون, ‘the beholders’); the passage may be corrupt or colloquial. I read: ‘lovelier than any beholders have seen’.

sentences.t: وَهِيَ لَا بِسَةٌ أَفْخَرَ الْمَلَابِسِ فَقَامَ أَخِي عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-hiya lā bisatun afkhara al-malābisi fa-qāma akhī ʿalā qadamayhi
sentences.l: And she (was) wearing the most splendid of garments; so rose my-brother upon his-two-feet.
sentences.i: She was dressed in the most splendid raiment, and my brother rose to his feet.
sentences.n: لا بسة is printed as two words; it is لابسة ‘wearing’. أفخر الملابس, ‘the most splendid of clothes’, is an accusative of the thing worn.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ ضَحِكَتْ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَفَرِحَتْ بِهِ وَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ بِالْجُلُوسِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾathu ḍaḥikat fī wajhihi wa-fariḥat bihi wa-ashārat ilayhi bi-al-julūsi
sentences.l: So when she-saw-him she-laughed in his-face, and was-glad with-him, and signalled to-him with-the-sitting.
sentences.i: When she saw him she smiled in his face, was glad of him, and signed to him to sit.
sentences.n: ضحكت في وجهه is a smile of greeting, ‘laughed to his face’.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَمَرَتْ بِالْبَابِ فَأُغْلِقَ ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَى أَخِي وَأَخَذَتْ يَدَهُ وَمَضَوْا جَمِيعًا إِلَى أَنْ أَتَوْا إِلَى حُجْرَةٍ مُنْفَرِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā amarat bi-al-bābi fa-ughliqa thumma aqbalat ʿalā akhī wa-akhadhat yadahu wa-maḍaw jamīʿan ilā an ataw ilā ḥujratin munfaridatin
sentences.l: Then indeed-she commanded about-the-door, so it-was-locked; then she-turned-toward my-brother, and took his-hand, and they-went all-together until they-came to a room, set-apart.
sentences.i: Then she gave an order about the door, and it was locked. She turned to my brother, took his hand, and they went on together until they came to a chamber apart.
sentences.n: أمرت بالباب, ‘she commanded as to the door’, is an order to shut it; the passive فأغلق follows at once.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَاهَا وَإِذَا هِيَ مَفْرُوشَةٌ بِأَنْوَاعِ الدِّيبَاجِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalāhā wa-idhā hiya mafrūshatun bi-anwāʿi al-dībājī
sentences.l: So they-both-entered-it; and behold, it (was) spread with kinds of brocade.
sentences.i: They went in, and found it spread with every kind of brocade.
sentences.n: دخلاها is the dual: the two of them, he and the girl.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَ أَخِي وَجَلَسَتْ بِجَانِبِهِ وَلَا عَبَتْهُ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-jalasa akhī wa-jalasat bi-jānibihi wa-lā ʿabathu sāʿatan
sentences.l: So sat my-brother, and she-sat at his-side, and she-played-with-him an hour.
sentences.i: My brother sat, and she sat beside him and dallied with him for an hour.
sentences.n: ولا عبته is printed as two words; it is ولاعبته, ‘she toyed, played with him’ (III lāʿaba), here an amorous sport. ساعة ‘an hour’ is loosely ‘a while’.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَا تَبْرَحْ مِنْ مَكَانِكَ حَتَّى أَجِيْ
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat wa-qālat lahu lā tabraḥ min makānika ḥattā ajī
sentences.l: Then she-rose and said to-him: “Do-not depart from your-place until I-come.”
sentences.i: Then she rose and said to him, “Do not stir from your place until I return.”
sentences.n: In the print the yāʾ of أجي carries a sukūn, which I keep: أجيْ for أجيء, ‘I come’, with the hamza dropped, as in speech.

sentences.t: وَغَابَتْ عَنْ أَخِي سَاعَةً فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ كَذَلِكَ إِذْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ عَبْدٌ أَسْوَدُ عَظِيمُ الْخِلْقَةِ وَمَعَهُ سَيْفٌ مُجَرَّدٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ghābat ʿan akhī sāʿatan fa-baynamā huwa ka-dhālika idh dakhala ʿalayhi ʿabdun aswadu ʿaẓīmu al-khilqati wa-maʿahu sayfun mujarradun
sentences.l: And she-was-absent from my-brother an hour; and while he (was) thus, lo, entered upon-him a slave, black, great (of) the-build, and with-him a sword, drawn.
sentences.i: She was gone from my brother an hour; and while he sat so, in came a black slave of enormous build, a drawn sword in his hand.
sentences.n: عظيم الخلقة, ‘great of build’, is a ‘bahuvrihi’-type annexation: an adjective governing a noun in the genitive.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ وَمَنْ جَاءَ بِكَ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ وَمَا الَّذِي تَصْنَعُ هَهُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu waylaka wa-man jāʾa bika ilā hādhā al-makāni wa-mā alladhī taṣnaʿu hahunā
sentences.l: So he-said to-him: “Woe to-you! and who brought you to this place, and what (is) the-thing you-do here?”
sentences.i: He said to him, “Woe to you! Who brought you to this place, and what are you doing here?”
sentences.n: جاء بك, ‘came with you’, is the common ‘brought you’. ما الذي تصنع is ‘what is it that you do’.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَخِي أَنْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْهِ جَوَابًا وَانْعَقَدَ لِسَانُهُ عَنْ رَدِّ الْجَوَابِ فَأَخَذَهُ وَعَرَّاهُ مِنْ أَثْوَابِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu lam yaqdir akhī an yarudda ʿalayhi jawāban wa-inʿaqada lisānuhu ʿan raddi al-jawābi fa-akhadhahu wa-ʿarrāhu min athwābihi
sentences.l: So when he-saw-him my-brother was-not-able to-answer upon-him an answer, and his-tongue was-knotted from the-returning of-the-reply; so he-seized-him and stripped-him of his-garments.
sentences.i: When my brother saw him he could not give him an answer; his tongue was tied and would not frame a reply. The slave seized him, stripped him of his clothes,
sentences.n: رد جوابا, ‘return an answer’, is the usual way to say ‘reply’. The sentence runs on into the next sentence.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَضْرِبُهُ بِالسَّيْفِ سَطْحًا إِلَى أَنْ سَقَطَ إِلَى الأَرْضِ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal yaḍribuhu bi-al-sayfi saṭḥan ilā an saqaṭa ilā al-arḍi maghshiyyan ʿalayhi min shiddati al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: And he-did-not cease striking-him with-the-sword, flat-wise, until he-fell to the-ground, fainted upon-him, from the-severity of-the-beating.
sentences.i: and went on beating him with the flat of the sword until he fell to the ground senseless from the violence of the blows.
sentences.n: سطحا, literally ‘flatly’, I take as ‘with the flat of the blade’ (Lane gives سَطَحَهُ ‘he threw him on his back’); the word is not certain. مغشيا عليه is ‘covered over upon’, the standard ‘in a swoon’.

sentences.t: وَاعْتَقَدَ الْعَبْدُ النَّحْسُ أَنَّهُ قُضِيَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-iʿtaqada al-ʿabdu al-naḥsu annahu quḍiya ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And he-believed, the slave, the ill-omened, that it-had-been-decreed upon-him.
sentences.i: and the accursed slave believed that he had finished him off.
sentences.n: قضي عليه, ‘it was decreed upon him’, is the idiom for ‘he was done for’, dead. النحس, ‘the ill-omened’, is a stock epithet for the slave.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَهُ أَخِي يَقُولُ أَيْنَ الْمَمْلَحَةُ فَأَ قْبَلَتْ إِلَيْهِ جَارِيَةٌ فِي يَدِهَا طَبَقٌ كَبِيرٌ وَفِيهِ مِلْحٌ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿahu akhī yaqūlu ayna al-mamlaḥatu fa-a qbalat ilayhi jāriyatun fī yadihā ṭabaqun kabīrun wa-fīhi milḥun kathīrun
sentences.l: And my-brother heard him saying: “Where (is) the salt-cellar?” — and there-came to-him a girl, in her-hand a tray, big, and in-it salt, much.
sentences.i: Then my brother heard him say, “Where is the salt-cellar?” A slave-girl came to him with a large tray in her hand, heaped with salt.
sentences.n: المملحة, a salt-cellar or salting-vessel, is a word I cannot confirm in the lexica; ‘salt-cellar’ is the sense the next lines demand. فا قبلت is printed as two words, فأقبلت ‘and she came’.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْعَبْدُ يَحْشُو جِرَاحَاتِ أَخِي وَهُوَ لَا يَتَحَرَّكُ خِيفَةً أَنْ يَعْلَمَ أَنَّهُ حَيٌّ فَيَقْتُلَهُ وَيُرَوِّحَ رُوحَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-ʿabdu yaḥshū jirāḥāti akhī wa-huwa lā yataḥarraku khīfatan an yaʿlama annahu ḥayyun fa-yaqtulahu wa-yurawwiḥa rūḥahu
sentences.l: And the slave did-not cease stuffing the-wounds of-my-brother, while he (did) not move, in-fear that he-should-learn that he (was) alive, and so-kill-him and send-off his-spirit.
sentences.i: The slave went on packing the salt into my brother’s wounds, while my brother lay without a movement, for fear that the man would find him alive, kill him, and dispatch his soul.
sentences.n: ويروح روحه: I take يُرَوِّحَ as II rawwaḥa, ‘to send off, make go away’, an idiom in which the soul is dispatched; the print is colloquial and the reading is uncertain (يَرُوحَ رُوحُهُ, ‘his soul would depart’, is the other option).

sentences.t: قَٰلَ الرَّاوِي ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ مَضَتْ وَصَاحَ الْعَبْدُ وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْمُسَرْدِيبَةِ
sentences.tr: qāla al-rāwī thumma inna al-jāriyata maḍat wa-ṣāḥa al-ʿabdu wa-qāla ibnu al-musardībati
sentences.l: Said the-narrator: then indeed the girl went-off, and the slave cried-out and said: “Son of the Musardība!”
sentences.i: The narrator says: then the girl went away, and the slave cried out, “Son of the Musardība!”
sentences.n: قل is the edition’s defective spelling of قال; the dagger alif restores the reading. ابن المسرديبة is obscure: it may be an insult or a call to the old woman, and the word may come from سرداب ‘cellar’, but I cannot make it out and give it as printed.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَتِ الْعَجُوزُ إِلَى أَخِي وَجَرَّتْهُ مِنْ رِجْلِهِ إِلَى سِرْدَابٍ فَرَمَتْهُ فِيهِ عَلَى جَمَاعَةِ قَتْلَى
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾati al-ʿajūzu ilā akhī wa-jarrathu min rijlihi ilā sirdābin fa-ramathu fīhi ʿalā jamāʿati qatlā
sentences.l: Then came the old-woman to my-brother, and dragged-him by his-foot to a cellar, and threw-him in-it upon a company of slain.
sentences.i: Then the old woman came to my brother, dragged him by the foot to a cellar, and flung him down on a heap of the slain.
sentences.n: من رجله, ‘from his foot’, is ‘by his foot’.

sentences.t: فَأَقَامَ مَقَامَهُ يَوْمَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ جَعَلَ الْمِلْحَ سَبَبَ حَيَاتِهِ لِأَنَّهُ قَطَعَ الدَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-aqāma maqāmahu yawmayni kāmilayni wa-kāna Allāhu jaʿala al-milḥa sababa ḥayātihi li-annahu qaṭaʿa al-dama
sentences.l: So he-stayed in-his-place two days, complete; and God had made the salt the-cause of-his-life, because it cut the-blood.
sentences.i: There he lay, in the place where he had fallen, two whole days. God, it seems, had made the salt the cause of his life, for it stopped the bleeding.
sentences.n: وكان الله جعل is a pluperfect, ‘God had made’: kāna + a perfect. قطع الدم, ‘cut the blood’, means ‘staunched the flow’.

sentences.t: فَرَأَى أَخِي فِي نَفْسِهِ الْقُوَّةَ عَلَى الْحَرَكَةِ فَقَامَ أَخِي مِنَ السِّرْدَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾā akhī fī nafsihi al-quwwata ʿalā al-ḥarakati fa-qāma akhī min al-sirdābi
sentences.l: Then my-brother saw in himself the-strength for the-movement; so my-brother rose from the-cellar.
sentences.i: Then my brother felt strength in himself to move, and he rose out of the cellar,
sentences.n: في نفسه is ‘in himself’.

sentences.t: وَفَتَحَ طَابِقَهُ وَهُوَ خَائِفٌ وَخَرَجَ إِلَى بَرٍّ وَأَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ السِّتْرَ
sentences.tr: wa-fataḥa ṭābiqahu wa-huwa khāʾifun wa-kharaja ilā barrin wa-aʿṭāhu Allāhu al-sitra
sentences.l: And he-opened its-trap-door, while he (was) afraid, and went-out to open-country, and God gave-him the-covering.
sentences.i: and, in fear, he opened its hatch and came out into the open, and God granted him concealment.
sentences.n: طابقه, ‘its tabiq’, I take for the hatch or trap-door of the cellar (Lane lists ṭābaq for a brick or a layer); uncertain. بر is open ground, the outside. ستر, ‘covering’, is protection, concealment.

sentences.t: فَمَشَى فِي الظَّلَامِ وَاخْتَفَى فِي ذَلِكَ الْهَلِيزِ إِلَى الصُّبْحِ
sentences.tr: fa-mashā fī al-ẓalāmi wa-ikhtafā fī dhālika al-halīzi ilā al-ṣubḥi
sentences.l: So he-walked in the-darkness, and hid in that vestibule till the-morning.
sentences.i: He walked on through the dark and hid in that entrance-passage until morning.
sentences.n: الهليز is the colloquial form of دِهْلِيز, an entrance-passage or vestibule.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ وَقْتُ الصَّبَاحِ خَرَجَتْ تِلْكَ الْعَجُوزُ الْمَلْعُونَةُ فِي طَلَبِ صَيْدٍ آخَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna waqtu al-ṣabāḥi kharajat tilka al-ʿajūzu al-malʿūnatu fī ṭalabi ṣaydin ākhara
sentences.l: So when it-was the-time of-the-morning went-out that old-woman, the cursed, in search of prey, another.
sentences.i: When the hour of morning came, that accursed old woman went out in quest of other game,
sentences.n: صيد, ‘game’, ‘quarry’, is the old woman’s word for her victims.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ أَخِي فِي إِثْرِهَا وَهِيَ لَا تَعْلَمُ حَتَّى أَتَى إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja akhī fī ithrihā wa-hiya lā taʿlamu ḥattā atā ilā manzilihi
sentences.l: and my-brother went-out in her-track while she (did) not know, until he-came to his-house.
sentences.i: and my brother went out on her trail without her knowing, until he came to his own house.
sentences.n: في إثرها, ‘in her track’, is ‘behind her’. The sentence is the same as the previous one in the Arabic; I cut it at the change of subject.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يُعَالِجُ نَفْسَهُ حَتَّى بَرِئَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal yuʿāliju nafsahu ḥattā bariʾa
sentences.l: And he-did-not cease treating himself, until he-was-healed.
sentences.i: and he tended himself without ceasing until he was healed.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ يَتَعَهَّدُ الْعَجُوزَ وَيَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا كُلَّ وَقْتٍ وَهِيَ تَأْخُذُ النَّاسَ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa yataʿahhadu al-ʿajūza wa-yanẓuru ilayhā kulla waqtin wa-hiya takhudhu al-nāsa
sentences.l: And he (was) watching-over the old-woman and looking at-her every time, while she (was) taking the-people…
sentences.i: Meanwhile he kept watch on the old woman, looking at her at all times, while she led people off…
sentences.n: The sentence runs on: وهي تاخذ الناس (‘while she takes the people’, i.e. leads off her victims) continues in the next line. يتعهد, ‘look after, keep an eye on’, is used here for watching her closely.

sentences.t: وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا وَتُؤَدِّيهِمْ إِلَى تِلْكَ الدَّارِ وَأَخِي لَا يَنْطِقُ بِشَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: wāḥidan wāḥidan wa-tuʾaddīhim ilā tilka al-dāri wa-akhī lā yanṭiqu bi-shayʾin
sentences.l: one by one, and she-delivers-them to that house, and my brother not speaking with a thing.
sentences.i: one by one, and brought them to that house, while my brother said not a word.
sentences.n: تُؤَدِّيهِمْ is the old woman’s action, continuing the previous sentence: ‘she delivers them’.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَمَّا رَجَعَتْ إِلَيْهِ رُوحُهُ وَقُوَّتُهُ عَمَدَ إِلَى خِرْقَةٍ وَعَمِلَ مِنْهَا كِيسًا وَمَلَاءَهُ زُجَاجًا وَشَدَّهُ فِي وَسَطِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma lammā rajaʿat ilayhi rūḥuhu wa-quwwatuhu ʿamada ilā khirqatin wa-ʿamila minhā kīsan wa-malāʾahu zujājan wa-shaddahu fī wasaṭihi
sentences.l: Then when there-returned to-him his-spirit and-his-strength, he-set-out to a rag, and made from-it a bag, and filled-it (with) glass, and bound-it at his-middle.
sentences.i: Then, when his spirit and his strength had come back to him, he took a rag, made a bag of it, filled it with glass, and tied it about his waist.
sentences.n: The verb رَجَعَتْ is feminine and agrees with the nearer subject, رُوحُهُ, which can be feminine; the bag of glass is evidently meant to pass for a purse of coin. مَلَاءَهُ is the printed spelling of مَلَأَهُ, 'he filled it'.

sentences.t: وَتَنَكَّرَ حَتَّى لَا يَعْرِفَهُ أَحَدٌ وَلَبِسَ ثِيَابَ الْعَجَمِ وَأَخَذَ سَيْفًا وَجَعَلَهُ تَحْتَ ثِيَابِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-tanakkara ḥattā lā yaʿrifahu aḥadun wa-labisa thiyāba al-ʿajami wa-akhadha sayfan wa-jaʿalahu taḥta thiyābihi
sentences.l: And he-disguised-himself so-that not would-know-him anyone, and wore the-clothes of the-foreigners, and took a sword and put-it beneath his-clothes.
sentences.i: He disguised himself so that no one would know him, put on the clothes of the Persians, took a sword, and hid it beneath his garments.
sentences.n: الْعَجَمُ are the non-Arabs, in practice Persians; the 'foreigner's tongue' he speaks next is meant to match the clothes.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْعَجُوزَ قَالَ لَهَا بِلِسَانِ الْعَجَمِ يَا عَجُوزَانَا رَجُلٌ غَرِيبٌ وَصَلْتُ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى هَذَا الْبَلَدِ وَلَا أَعْرِفُ أَحَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-ʿajūza qāla lahā bi-lisāni al-ʿajami yā ʿajūzanā rajulun gharībun waṣaltu al-yawma ilā hādhā al-baladi wa-lā aʿrifu aḥadan
sentences.l: And when he-saw the-old-woman he-said to-her in the-tongue of-the-foreigners: O old-woman-I (am) a man, a stranger; I-arrived today at this city, and not I-know anyone.
sentences.i: When he saw the old woman he said to her, in the speech of the Persians, "Good mother, I am a stranger here. I reached this city only today, and I know no one in it."
sentences.n: عَجُوزَانَا is printed as one word: يا عجوز + أنا, 'O old woman — I (am)…'. The edition runs the words together, perhaps to suggest the foreigner's clipped Arabic; the vocative has no ending of its own, which is common in Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَهَلْ عِنْدَكِ مِيزَانٌ يَسَعُ تِسْعُمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ وَأَنَا أَهَبُكِ شَيْأً مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-hal ʿindaki mīzānun yasaʿu tisʿumiʾati dīnārin wa-anā ahabuki shayʾan minhu
sentences.l: So is-there with-you a balance that holds nine-hundred dinars? And I (will) give-you a thing of-it.
sentences.i: Have you a balance that will hold nine hundred dinars? I will give you a share of them for your pains.
sentences.n: أَهَبُكِ takes the woman as direct object; Classical would say أَهَبُ لَكِ. The foreigner's Arabic is deliberately a little off.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْعَجُوزُ لِي وَلَدٌ صَيْرَفِيٌّ وَعِنْدَهُ سَائِرُ الْمَوَازِينِ فَامْضِ مَعِي قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِ حَتَّى يَزِنَ ذَهَبَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-ʿajūzu lī waladun ṣayrafiyyun wa-ʿindahu sāʾiru al-mawāzīni fa-amḍi maʿī qabla an yakhruja min makānihi ḥattā yazina dhahabaka
sentences.l: And said to-him the-old-woman: To-me (is) a son, a money-changer, and with-him (are) all the-balances; so walk with-me before he-goes-out from his-place, so-that he-weigh your-gold.
sentences.i: The old woman said to him, "I have a son who is a money-changer, and he keeps every kind of scale. Come along with me before he leaves his shop, and he will weigh your gold."
sentences.n: سَائِرُ is 'all, the whole of' here (not 'the rest').

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي اِمْشِي قُدَّامِي فَسَارَتْ وَأَخِي خَلْفَهَا حَتَّى أَتَتِ الْبَابَ فَدَقَّتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī imshī quddāmī fa-sārat wa-akhī khalfahā ḥattā atati al-bāba fa-daqqathu
sentences.l: And said my-brother: Walk before-me. So she-walked, and my-brother behind-her, until she-came-to the-door, and she-knocked-it.
sentences.i: My brother said, "Walk in front of me." So she walked on, with my brother behind her, until she reached the door and knocked.
sentences.n: قُدَّامِي is the colloquial-leaning 'in front of me' (Classical أَمَامِي).

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ بِعَيْنِهَا وَفَتَحَتِ الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajati al-jāriyatu bi-ʿaynihā wa-fataḥati al-bāba
sentences.l: And went-out the-girl herself-in-person, and opened the-door.
sentences.i: Out came the very same girl, and she opened the door.
sentences.n: بِعَيْنِهَا, literally 'by her own eye', means 'the very one, in person': the same slave-girl who had lured him before.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَتِ الْعَجُوزُ فِي وَجْهِهَا فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ قَدْ أَتَيْتُكُمُ الْيَوْمَ بِلَحْمَةٍ سَمِينَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥikati al-ʿajūzu fī wajhihā fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu qad ataytukumu al-yawma bi-laḥmatin samīnatin
sentences.l: And laughed the-old-woman in her-face, and said the-old-woman: I-have-come-to-you today with a piece-of-meat, a fat one.
sentences.i: The old woman laughed in her face and said, "Today I have brought you a fine, fat piece of meat."
sentences.n: 'Meat' is the old woman's slang for the victim she has brought, and the laugh shows the girl understands her.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ بِيَدِ أَخِي وَأَدْ خَلَتْهُ الْمَنْزِلَ الَّذِي دَخَلَ أَخِي فِيهِ سَابِقًا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhati al-jāriyatu bi-yadi akhī wa-ad khalathu al-manzila alladhī dakhala akhī fīhi sābiqan
sentences.l: And took the-girl by the-hand of-my-brother, and brought-him-in the-dwelling in-which entered my-brother previously.
sentences.i: The girl took my brother by the hand and brought him into the same house he had entered once before.
sentences.n: The edition prints واد خلته as two words; it is one word, وأدخلته, 'and she brought him in', and is read as if joined. الْمَنْزِلَ الَّذِي دَخَلَ أَخِي فِيهِ is the same house, with a resumptive فِيهِ, 'in which'.

sentences.t: وَقَعَدَتْ عِنْدَهُ سَاعَةً وَقَامَتْ وَقَالَتْ لِأَخِي لَا تَبْرَحْ حَتَّى أَرْجِعَ إِلَيْكَ وَرَاحَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-qaʿadat ʿindahu sāʿatan wa-qāmat wa-qālat li-akhī lā tabraḥ ḥattā arjiʿa ilayka wa-rāḥat
sentences.l: And she-sat with-him an-hour, and rose, and said to-my-brother: Do-not leave until I-return to-you. And she-went-off.
sentences.i: She sat beside him for a while, then rose and said to my brother, "Do not stir from here until I come back to you." And she went off.
sentences.n: The printed لاخي is written with a bare alif: لِأَخِي, 'to my brother'.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ أَخِي إِلَّا وَالْعَبْدُ الْمَلْعُونُ أَقْبَلَ وَمَعَهُ السَّيْفُ الْمُجَرَّدُ وَقَالَ لِأَخِي قُمْ يَا مَلْعُونُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yashʿur akhī illā wa-al-ʿabdu al-malʿūnu aqbala wa-maʿahu al-sayfu al-mujarradu wa-qāla li-akhī qum yā malʿūnu
sentences.l: And not felt my-brother (anything) except-that the-slave, the-accursed, had-come-on, and with-him the-sword, the-drawn; and he-said to-my-brother: Rise, O accursed!
sentences.i: Before my brother knew it, the accursed slave was upon him with a drawn sword in his hand, crying, "Get up, you accursed wretch!"
sentences.n: فَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ … إِلَّا وَ… is the idiom 'he was not aware, but (suddenly) …'. The vocative يَا مَلْعُونُ is left in the nominative, as the edition's plain يا ملعون suggests.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَخِي وَتَقَدَّمَ الْعَبْدُ أَمَامَهُ وَأَخِي وَرَاءَهُ وَمَدَّيَدَهُ إِلَى سَيْفِهِ الَّذِي تَحْتَ ثِيَابِهِ وَضَرَبَهُ الْعَبْدَ فَأَطَاحَ رَأْسَهُ عَنْ بَدَنِهِ وَسَحَبَهُ مِنْ رِجْلِهِ إِلَى السِّرْدَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma akhī wa-taqaddama al-ʿabdu amāmahu wa-akhī warāʾahu wa-maddayadahu ilā sayfihi alladhī taḥta thiyābihi wa-ḍarabahu al-ʿabda fa-aṭāḥa raʾsahu ʿan badanihi wa-saḥabahu min rijlihi ilā al-sirdābi
sentences.l: And rose my-brother, and advanced the-slave before-him, and my-brother behind-him; and he-stretched-his-hand to his-sword that (was) under his-clothes, and struck-him, the-slave, and sent-flying his-head from his-body, and dragged-him by his-foot to the-cellar.
sentences.i: My brother rose, and the slave walked ahead of him with my brother at his back. Then my brother put his hand to the sword beneath his clothes and struck the slave, sending his head flying from his body, and dragged him by the foot down to the cellar.
sentences.n: ومديده is printed as one word: وَمَدَّ يَدَهُ, 'and he stretched out his hand'. وَضَرَبَهُ الْعَبْدَ has a pleonastic object, 'struck him — the slave'; the text may have dropped a word, but the reading is clear. السِّرْدَاب is a cellar or underground chamber.

sentences.t: وَنَادَى أَيْنَ الْمُمَلِّحَةُ فَجَاءَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَمَعَهَا الطَّبَقُ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْمِلْحُ فَلَمَّارَأَتْ أَخِي وَالسَّيْفُ بِيَدِهِ وَلَّتْ هَارِبَةً فَتَبِعَهَا وَضَرَبَهَا أَطَاحَ رَأْسَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-nādā ayna al-mumalliḥatu fa-jāʾati al-jāriyatu wa-maʿahā al-ṭabaqu alladhī fīhi al-milḥu fa-lammāraʾat akhī wa-al-sayfu bi-yadihi wallat hāribatan fa-tabiʿahā wa-ḍarabahā aṭāḥa raʾsahā
sentences.l: And he-called: Where (is) the-salt-cellar? So came the-girl, and with-her the-tray in-which (is) the-salt. And when-she-saw my-brother, and the-sword in his-hand, she-turned fleeing; so he-followed-her and struck-her, sent-flying her-head.
sentences.i: Then my brother cried out, "Where is the salt-cellar?" and the girl came with the tray that held the salt. But when she saw my brother with the sword in his hand, she turned and fled. He ran after her, struck her, and sent her head flying.
sentences.n: الْمُمَلِّحَة is printed with a different vowel pattern from the earlier مَمْلَحَة; I read it as the same call (the salt-cellar), though ‘the woman who salts’ is possible. فَلَمَّارَأَتْ is printed as one word. ضَرَبَهَا أَطَاحَ رَأْسَهَا has no wa- between the two verbs (asyndeton: ‘struck her, sent her head flying’).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَادَى أَيْنَ الْعَجُوزُ فَجَاءَتْ فَقَالَ لَهَا أَتَعْرِفِينَنِي يَا عَجُوزَ النَّحْسِ
sentences.tr: thumma nādā ayna al-ʿajūzu fa-jāʾat fa-qāla lahā a-taʿrifīnanī yā ʿajūza al-naḥsi
sentences.l: Then he-called: Where (is) the-old-woman? So she-came, and he-said to-her: Do-you-know-me, O old-woman of-ill-luck?
sentences.i: Then he called, "Where is the old woman?" She came, and he said to her, "Do you know me, you hag of ill omen?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَا يَامَوْلَايَ فَقَالَ لَهَا أَنَا صَاحِبُ الدَّرَاهِمِ الَّتِي جِئْتِ عِنْدِي وَ تَوَضَّأْتِ عِنْدِي وَصَايَتِ فِيهَا وَأَوْقَعْتِنِي هُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lā yāmawlāya fa-qāla lahā anā ṣāḥibu al-darāhimi allatī jiʾti ʿindī wa-tawaḍḍaʾti ʿindī wa-ṣāyati fīhā wa-awqaʿtinī hunā
sentences.l: And she-said: No, O-my-master. And he-said to-her: I (am) the-owner of-the-dirhams that you-came with-me, and you-made-ablution with-me, and you-prayed in-it, and you-made-me-fall here.
sentences.i: "No, my lord," she said. He said to her, "I am the man with the dirhams, the one you came to, and washed for prayer in his house, and prayed there, and so brought down on me this fate here."
sentences.n: يَامَوْلَايَ is printed as one word. الَّتِي جِئْتِ has no pronoun to return to الدَّرَاهِم, a loose Middle Arabic relative; the sense is that she came to him over the dirhams, as part of her pious pretence. The lone وَ before تَوَضَّأْتِ is a stray word-space in the print. وَصَايَتِ must be a spelling of وَصَلَّيْتِ, 'you prayed', but the form is odd and may be corrupt; فِيهَا refers back to the house or the place of prayer.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ اِتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَتَرَاجَعْ فِي أَمْرِي فَلَمْ يَلْتَفِتْ إِلَيْهَا وَضَرَبَهَا حَتَّى قَطَعَهَا أَرْبَعَ قِطَعٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati ittaqi Allāha wa-tarājaʿ fī amrī fa-lam yaltafit ilayhā wa-ḍarabahā ḥattā qaṭaʿahā arbaʿa qiṭaʿin
sentences.l: And she-said: Fear God, and draw-back in my-affair. But he-did-not turn to-her, and struck-her until he-cut-her four pieces.
sentences.i: She said, "Fear God, and relent in my case." But he paid her no heed; he struck her until he had cut her into four pieces.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَ فِي طَلَبِ الْجَارِيَةِ فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ طَارَ عَقْلُهَا وَقَالَتِ الْأَمَانَ فَأَمَّنَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma kharaja fī ṭalabi al-jāriyati fa-lammā raʾathu ṭāra ʿaqluhā wa-qālati al-amāna fa-ammanahā
sentences.l: Then he-went-out in search of-the-girl; and when-she-saw-him, her-mind flew, and she-said: The-quarter! And he-granted-her-quarter.
sentences.i: Then he went out to look for the girl, and when she saw him her wits flew from her, and she cried, "Mercy!" and he granted her mercy.
sentences.n: الْأَمَانَ is the cry for quarter, safe-conduct; he answers with فَأَمَّنَهَا, 'and he gave her it'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا مَا الَّذِي أَوْقَعَكِ عِنْدَ هَذَا الْأَسْوَدِ فَقَالَتْ إِنِّي كُنْتُ جَارِيَةً لِبَعْضِ التُّجَّارِ وَكَانَتْ هَذِهِ الْعَجُوزُ تَتَرَدَّدُ عَلَيَّ فَآنَسْتُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā mā alladhī awqaʿaki ʿinda hādhā al-aswadi fa-qālat innī kuntu jāriyatan li-baʿḍi al-tujjāri wa-kānat hādhihi al-ʿajūzu tataraddadu ʿalayya fa-ānastu bihā
sentences.l: And he-said to-her: What (is) that-which made-you-fall with this black-one? And she-said: Indeed-I was a slave-girl belonging-to some of-the-merchants, and this old-woman used-to frequent me, and I-grew-friendly with-her.
sentences.i: He said to her, "What brought you to be with this black man?" She said, "I was the slave-girl of one of the merchants, and this old woman used to visit me often, until I became fond of her."
sentences.n: عَلَيَّ here is 'upon me' in the sense of 'coming to see me'. أَنِسَ بِـ is 'to be at ease with, to take to someone'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِي يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ إِنَّ عِنْدَنَا فَرَحٌ مَارَى أَحَدٌ مِثْلَهُ وَقَدِ اشْتَهَيْتُ أَنْ تَنْظُرِي إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lī yawman min al-ayyāmi inna ʿindanā faraḥun mārā aḥadun mithlahu wa-qadi ishtahaytu an tanẓuri ilayhi
sentences.l: And she-said to-me one-day of the-days: Indeed with-us (is) a wedding-feast, not-saw anyone its-like; and I-have-wished that you-look at-it.
sentences.i: One day she said to me, "We are holding a feast the like of which no one has ever seen, and I should dearly like you to look upon it."
sentences.n: مَارَى is printed as one word, ما رأى, with the hamza dropped, as it would be spoken. فَرَح is a rejoicing, here a wedding feast.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً ثُمَّ قُمْتُ وَلَبِسْتُ أَحْسَنَ ثِيَابِي وَمَصَاغِي وَأَخَذْتُ مَعِي صُرَّةً فِيهَا مِائَةَ دِينَارٍ وَمَضَيْتُ مَعَهَا حَتَّى أَدْخَلَتْنِي هَذِهِ الدَّارَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan thumma qumtu wa-labistu aḥsana thiyābī wa-maṣāghī wa-akhadhtu maʿī ṣurratan fīhā miʾata dīnārin wa-maḍaytu maʿahā ḥattā adkhalatnī hādhihi al-dāra
sentences.l: And I-said to-her: Hearing and obedience. Then I-rose, and put-on the-best of-my-clothes and my-jewellery, and took with-me a purse in-it a-hundred dinars, and went with-her until she-brought-me-into this house.
sentences.i: I answered her with hearing and obedience. Then I got up, put on my finest clothes and my jewels, took with me a purse holding a hundred dinars, and went along with her until she brought me into this very house.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُ مَا شَعَرْتُ إِلَّاوَهَذَا الْأَسْوَدُ أَخَذَنِي وَأَنَا عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ ثَلٰثَ سِنِينَ بِحِيلَةِ الْعَجُوزِ الْمَلْعُونَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhaltu mā shaʿartu illāwa-hādhā al-aswadu akhadhanī wa-anā ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli thalātha sinīna bi-ḥīlati al-ʿajūzi al-malʿūnati
sentences.l: And when I-entered, not I-felt (anything) but-that this black-one had-seized-me, and I (have been) in this state three years, by the-trick of-the-old-woman, the-accursed.
sentences.i: No sooner had I entered than this black man seized me, and I have lived in this state for three years, through the cunning of that accursed old woman.
sentences.n: ثلث is the edition's defective spelling of ثلاث; it is pointed with a dagger alif (ثَلٰثَ) so that it reads 'three'. The girl's seizure is not spelled out; the sense of أَخَذَنِي here is that he took her by force and kept her.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا أَخِي هَلْ لَهُ فِي هَذِهِ الدَّارِ شَيْءءٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā akhī hal lahu fī hādhihi al-dāri shayʾun
sentences.l: And said to-her my-brother: Is-there to-him in this house a-thing?
sentences.i: My brother said to her, "Has he anything in this house?"
sentences.n: The edition prints شيءء with a doubled hamza, an evident slip for شيء; it reads shayʾ. The له is the slave's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ عِنْدَهُ شَيْ كَثِيرٌ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَقْدِرُ عَلَى نَقْلِهِ فَانْقُلْهُ وَاسْتَخِرِ اللَّهَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ʿindahu shay kathīrun fa-in kunta taqdiru ʿalā naqlihi fa-unqulhu wa-istakhiri Allāha
sentences.l: And she-said: With-him (is) a-thing, much; so if you-are able to its-carrying, then carry-it, and seek-the-best-from God.
sentences.i: She said, "He has a great deal. If you can carry it away, then carry it, and ask God to guide your choice."
sentences.n: شَيْ without hamza is the Middle Arabic spelling and pronunciation (shay) of شيء. اسْتَخِرِ اللَّهَ is the prayer of istikhāra, asking God to choose the better course.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَخِي وَمَشَى مَعَهَا وَفَتَحَتْ لَهُ صَنَادِيقَ فِيهَا أَكْيَاسٌ فَبَقِيَ أَخِي مُتَحَيِّرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma akhī wa-mashā maʿahā wa-fataḥat lahu ṣanādīqa fīhā akyāsun fa-baqiya akhī mutaḥayyiran
sentences.l: And rose my-brother and walked with-her, and she-opened for-him chests, in-them bags; and my-brother remained bewildered.
sentences.i: My brother rose and walked with her, and she opened chests for him that were full of bags, and he stood there bewildered.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْجَارِيَةُ اِمْضِ الْآنَ وَدَعْنِي هُنَا وَهَاتِ مَنْ يَنْقُلُ الْمَالَ فَخَرَجَ وَأَكْرَى عَشَرَةَ رِجَالٍ وَجَاءَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-jāriyatu imḍi al-āna wa-daʿnī hunā wa-hāti man yanqulu al-māla fa-kharaja wa-akrā ʿasharata rijālin wa-jāʾa
sentences.l: And said to-him the-girl: Go now, and leave-me here, and bring whoever will-carry the-money. So he-went-out, and hired ten men, and came.
sentences.i: The girl said to him, "Go now, leave me here, and fetch men to carry the money." So he went out, hired ten porters, and returned.

sentences.t: إِلَى الْبَابِ فَوَجَدَ مَفْتُوحًا وَلَاأَرَى الْجَارِيَةَ وَلَاالْأَكْيَاسَ إِلَّاشَيْئًا يَسِيرًا غَيْرَ الْقُمَاشِ
sentences.tr: ilā al-bābi fa-wajada maftūḥan wa-lā arā al-jāriyata wa-lā al-akyāsa illā shayʾan yasīran ghayra al-qumāshi
sentences.l: To the door; and he found (it) open, and not I-see the girl, nor the purses, except a small thing other-than the cloth.
sentences.i: He came to the door and found it standing open. Of the girl and the purses there was no sign, only some small thing besides the cloth.
sentences.n: This sentence begins at the door of the house. وَلَاأَرَى is printed with the particle and verb run together; as printed the verb is first person (“I see”), which does not suit the narration and may be a slip for yarā “sees”. We point it as printed and translate as the sense requires. Several words in this passage are printed run together (وَلَاالْأَكْيَاسَ, إِلَّاشَيْئًا); the vocalisation keeps them glued exactly as the edition does.

sentences.t: فَعَلِمَ أَنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ خَدَعَتْهُ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَخَذَ الْمَالَ الَّذِي بَقِيَ وَفَتَحَ الْخَزَائِنَ وَأَخَذَ مَافِيهَا وَلَمْ يَتْرُكْ فِي الدَّارِ شَئْاً وَبَاتَ مَسْرُورًا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿalima anna al-jāriyata khadaʿathu fa-ʿinda dhālika akhadha al-māla alladhī baqiya wa-fataḥa al-khazāʾina wa-akhadha māfīhā wa-lam yatruk fī al-dāri shayʾan wa-bāta masrūran
sentences.l: So he knew that the girl had deceived him; so at that he took the money that remained, and opened the storerooms, and took what-was-in them, and did not leave in the house a thing; and he spent-the-night gladdened.
sentences.i: Then he knew that the girl had tricked him. At that he took what money was left, opened the storerooms, took all that was in them, and left nothing in the house; and he passed the night in good cheer.
sentences.n: مَافِيهَا is printed as one word, “what is in them”. شياً is one of the few prose words that carries a printed mark (the tanwīn); the hamza on the yā’ is our addition.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَجَدَ بِالْبَابِ عِشْرِينَ جُنْدِيًّا تَعَلَّقُوا بِهِ وَقَالُوا لَهُ إِنَّ الْوَالِى يَطْلُبُكَ فَأَخَذُوهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wajada bi-al-bābi ʿishrīna jundiyyan taʿallaqū bihi wa-qālū lahu inna al-wālī yaṭlubuka fa-akhadhūhu
sentences.l: So when the morning became-morning, he found at the door twenty soldiers; they clung to him and said to him, “Indeed the governor seeks you”; so they seized him.
sentences.i: When morning broke he found twenty soldiers at his door. They laid hold of him and said, “The governor wants you.” And they seized him.
sentences.n: عِشْرِينَ جُنْدِيًّا: the noun after the numeral is accusative singular, as Classical grammar requires.

sentences.t: فَتَدَخَّلَ أَخِي عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَعْبُرَ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ فَلَمْ يُمْهِلُوهُ بِأَنْ يَرْجِعَ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ فَوَعَدَهُمْ بِجُمْلَةٍ مِنَ الدَّرَاهِمِ فَأَبَوْا
sentences.tr: fa-tadakhkhala akhī ʿalayhim li-yaʿbura ilā baytihi fa-lam yumhilūhu bi-an yarjiʿa ilā baytihi fa-waʿadahum bi-jumlatin min al-darāhimi fa-abaw
sentences.l: So my brother interceded upon them, that he might cross to his house; and they did not grant-him-respite that he return to his house; so he promised them a sum of dirhams; so they refused.
sentences.i: My brother pleaded with them to let him go over to his house, but they would not give him even the time to go back to it. He promised them a good sum of dirhams, yet they refused.
sentences.n: تَدَخَّلَ عَلَى is used here for “appeal to, plead with”, a Middle Arabic sense (Classical تَدَخَّلَ is “to intervene”). It recurs two sentences below.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَبَطُوهُ بِحَبْلٍ رَبْطًا شَدِ يدًا وَرَاحُوا بِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma rabaṭūhu bi-ḥablin rabṭan shadī-dan wa-rāḥū bihi
sentences.l: Then they bound him with a rope, a binding tight-ly, and they went off with him.
sentences.i: Then they bound him fast with a rope and marched him away.
sentences.n: The edition prints شد يدا as two words; it is شَدِيدًا “severe, tight” split by a spacing glitch. We keep the two tokens and pointed them so that they read together: shadī-dan.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدَ هُمْ فِى الطَّرِيقِ وَاحِدٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَتَعَلَّقَ أَخِي بِذَيْلِهِ وَتَدَخَّلَ عَلَيْهِ لِكَيْ يَقِفَ مَعَهُ وَيُسَاعِدَهُ عَلَى خَلَاصِهِ مِنْ أَيْدِيهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-wajada hum fī al-ṭarīqi wāḥidun min aṣḥābihi fa-taʿallaqa akhī bi-dhaylihi wa-tadakhkhala ʿalayhi li-kay yaqifa maʿahu wa-yusāʿidahu ʿalā khalāṣihi min aydīhim
sentences.l: So there found them, in the road, one of his companions; so my brother clung to his hem and interceded upon him, so-that he would stand with him and help him toward his deliverance from their hands.
sentences.i: On the road one of his friends came upon them, and my brother clung to the man’s skirt and begged him to stand by him and help to deliver him from their hands.
sentences.n: وَجَدَ هُمْ: the object pronoun is printed as a separate word. The verb comes before its subject, وَاحِدٌ, and is singular, which is the normal Classical order.

sentences.t: فَوَقَفَ الرَّجُلُ وَسَأَلَهُمْ عَنْ قِصَّتِهِ فَقَالُوا لَهُ إِنَّ الْوَالِيَ قَدْحَكَمَ عَلَيْنَا بِأَنْ نُحْضِرَهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهَا نَحْنُ ذَاهِبُونَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-waqafa al-rajulu wa-saʾalahum ʿan qiṣṣatihi fa-qālū lahu inna al-wālīya qadḥakama ʿalaynā bi-an nuḥḍirahu bayna yadayhi wahā naḥnu dhāhibūna bihi
sentences.l: So the man stood, and asked them about his story; so they said to him, “Indeed the governor has ruled upon us that we bring him between his hands; and here we are, going with him.”
sentences.i: The man stopped and asked them what his story was. They told him, “The governor has ordered us to bring him before him, and here we are taking him.”
sentences.n: قَدْحَكَمَ is printed as one word, qad ḥakama. بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, literally “between his hands”, is the stock phrase for “into his presence”.

sentences.t: فَالْتَمَسَ، لَهُمْ صَاحِبُ أَخِي بِأَنْ يُخَلِّصُوهُ وَيُعْطِيهِمْ خَمْسَ مِائَةِ دِينَارٍ وَقَالَ لَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ إِلَى الْوَالِي فَقُولُوا لَهُ مَالَقِينَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-iltamasa, lahum ṣāḥibu akhī bi-an yukhalliṣūhu wa-yuʿṭī-him khamsa miʾati dīnārin wa-qāla lahum idhā rajaʿtum ilā al-wālī fa-qūlū lahu mā laqīnāhu
sentences.l: So he requested, of them, the companion of my brother, that they free him, and he gives them five hundred dinars; and he said to them, “When you return to the governor, say to him, ‘We did not meet him.’”
sentences.i: My brother’s friend then begged them to let him go, offering them five hundred dinars, and said, “When you go back to the governor, tell him that you never found him.”
sentences.n: The comma after فَالْتَمَسَ is the edition’s own. وَيُعْطِيهِمْ is indicative where Classical grammar would expect the subjunctive after بِأَنْ; we point it as printed, reading it as “and he would give them”. مَالَقِينَاهُ is printed as one word: mā + perfect, “we did not meet him”.

sentences.t: فَأَعْرَضُوا عَنْ كَلَامِهِ وَأَخَذُوهُ مَسْحُوبًا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ حَتَّى أَحْضَرُوهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ الْوَالِي
sentences.tr: fa-aʿraḍū ʿan kalāmihi wa-akhadhūhu masḥūban ʿalā wajhihi ḥattā aḥḍarūhu bayna yadayi al-wālī
sentences.l: So they turned away from his speech, and took him dragged upon his face, until they brought him between the hands of the governor.
sentences.i: They paid no heed to what he said, but dragged him along on his face until they brought him before the governor.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْوَالِي أَخِي قَالَ لَهُ مِنْ أَيْنَ لَكَ هَذَا الْقُمَاشُ وَالْمَالُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-wālī akhī qāla lahu min ayna laka hādhā al-qumāshu wa-al-mālu
sentences.l: So when the governor saw my brother, he said to him, “From where (is) to you this cloth and the money?”
sentences.i: When the governor saw my brother he said to him, “Where did you come by this cloth and this money?”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي أُرِيدُ الْأَمَانَ فَأَعْطَاهُ مِنْدِيلَ الْأَمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī urīdu al-amānia fa-aʿṭāhu mindīla al-amāni
sentences.l: So my brother said, “I want the safe-conduct”; so he gave him the handkerchief of the safe-conduct.
sentences.i: “Grant me safe-conduct,” said my brother; and the governor gave him the handkerchief of safety.
sentences.n: مِنْدِيلُ الْأَمَانِ, “the handkerchief of safety”, was the token by which a ruler pledged that a man would come to no harm while he spoke.

sentences.t: فَحَدَّثَهُ بِمَاجَرَى وَمَاوَقَعَ لَهُ مَعَ الْعَجُوزِ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ وَهُرُوبِ الْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaddathahu bi-mā jarā wa-mā waqaʿa lahu maʿa al-ʿajūzi min al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri wa-hurūbi al-jāriyati
sentences.l: So he related to him what had happened, and what had befallen him with the old woman, from the first to the last, and the flight of the girl.
sentences.i: So he told him all that had happened to him with the old woman, from first to last, and how the girl had fled.
sentences.n: بِمَاجَرَى and وَمَاوَقَعَ are printed run together (bi-mā jarā, wa-mā waqaʿa).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلْوَالِي وَالَّذِي أَخَذْتَهُ خُذْ مِنْهُ مَاشِئْتَ وَدَعْ لِي مَا أَتَقَوَّتُ بِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-wālī wa-alladhī akhadhtahu khudh minhu mā shiʾta wa-daʿ lī mā ataqawwatu bihi
sentences.l: Then he said to the governor, “And that-which you have taken, take from it what you will, and leave to me what I sustain-myself with.”
sentences.i: Then he said to the governor, “As for what you have taken, take of it whatever you please, but leave me enough to live on.”
sentences.n: مَاشِئْتَ is printed as one word, mā shiʾta, “what you wished”.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْوَالِى الْقُمَاشَ وَالْمَالَ كُلَّهُ وَخَشِيَ أَنْ يَبْلُغَ الْخَبَرُ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ فَأَحْضَرَ أَخِي وَقَالَ لَهُ اُخْرُجْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَإِلَّاشَنَقَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-wālī al-qumāsha wa-al-māla kullahu wa-khashiya an yablugha al-khabaru ilā al-sulṭāni fa-aḥḍara akhī wa-qāla lahu ukhruj min hādhihi al-madīnati wa-illā shanaqaka
sentences.l: So the governor took the cloth and the money, all of it, and feared that the news would reach the sultan; so he had my brother brought, and said to him, “Go out from this city, and if-not, hanged-you (he).”
sentences.i: The governor took the cloth and all the money, and, fearing that word of it would reach the sultan, he sent for my brother and said to him, “Leave this city, or you will be hanged.”
sentences.n: وَإِلَّاشَنَقَكَ is printed as one word, wa-illā shanaqaka, with the perfect in a threat (“otherwise he hanged you”), as Middle Arabic often has it. The subject is unexpressed: the printed letters suggest “he [the sultan] hangs you”, though a lost alif could also give wa-illā ashnuqka “or I hang you”. We point the letters as they stand.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ فَخَرَجَ إِلَى بَعْضِ الْبُلْدَانِ فَخَرَجَتْ عَلَيْهِ اللُّصُوصُ فَعَرَّوْهُ وَضَرَبُوهُ وَقَطَعُوا أُذُنَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu fa-kharaja ilā baʿḍi al-buldāni fa-kharajat ʿalayhi al-luṣūṣu fa-ʿarrawhu wa-ḍarabūhu wa-qaṭaʿū udhunayhi
sentences.l: So he said, “The hearing and the obedience”; so he went out to some of the lands; so the thieves came out upon him, and stripped him, and beat him, and cut off his ears.
sentences.i: “With hearing and obedience,” he said, and went off to one of the provinces. There robbers fell upon him, stripped him, beat him, and cut off both his ears.
sentences.n: السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ is the courtier’s formula of submission, here said under threat of hanging.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعْتُ بِخَبَرِهِ فَخَرَجْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَأَخَذْتُ إِلَيْهِ ثِيَابًا وَجِئْتُ بِهِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ سِرًّا وَرَتَّبْتُ لَهُ مَا يَأْ كُلُ كُلَّ وَمَا يَشْرَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿtu bi-khabarihi fa-kharajtu ilayhi wa-akhadhtu ilayhi thiyāban wa-jiʾtu bihi ilā al-madīnati sirran wa-rattabtu lahu mā yaʾ kullu kulla wa-mā yashrabu
sentences.l: So I heard of his news, so I went out to him, and took to him clothes, and brought him to the city secretly, and arranged for him what he eats, all, and what he drinks.
sentences.i: I heard of what had befallen him, went out to him with clothes, and brought him back to the city in secret, and I provided for all that he should eat and drink.
sentences.n: Here the narrator, the barber, speaks in the first person. In مَا يَأْ كُلُ كُلَّ the edition splits the verb yaʾkulu into two words and then prints كل again. The second كل may be a printer’s repeat, or may stand for كل يوم “every day”; we read it as kulla “all” and let the translation absorb it.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَخِي السَّادِسُ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَهُوَ مَقْطُوعُ الشَّفَتَيْنِ فَكَانَ افْتَقَرَ فَخَرَجَ يَوْمًا يَطْلُبُ شَيْئًا يَسْلُبُهُ رَمَقَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā akhī al-sādisu yā amīra al-muʾminīna wa-huwa maqṭūʿu al-shafatayni fa-kāna iftaqara fa-kharaja yawman yaṭlubu shayʾan yaslubuhu ramaqahu
sentences.l: And as-for my brother, the sixth, O commander of the believers — and he (is) cut-off of the two lips — he had become poor; so he went out one day seeking something (that) strips his last-breath.
sentences.i: As for my sixth brother, O Commander of the Faithful — he whose lips were cut off — he had fallen into poverty, and one day he went out looking for something to keep body and soul together.
sentences.n: يَسْلُبُهُ رَمَقَهُ is printed as given and would mean “strips him of his last breath”. The usual phrase is يَسُدُّ بِهِ رَمَقَهُ “with which to stay his hunger”, and the text is probably corrupt here; the translation follows the likely sense. The two brothers’ stories are told as the barber’s own, to the caliph, which is why the address يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ (printed as one word) is there.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ فِي بَعْضِ الطُّرُقِ إِذْرَى دَارًا حَسَنَةً وَلَهَا دِهْلِيزٌ وَاسِعٌ مُرْتَفِعٌ وَعَلَى الْبَابِ خَدَمٌ وَأَمْرٌ وَنَهْيٌ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa fī baʿḍi al-ṭuruqi idh-rā dāran ḥasanatan wa-lahā dihlīzun wāsiʿun murtafiʿun wa-ʿalā al-bābi khadamun wa-amrun wa-nahyun
sentences.l: So while he (was) in some of the roads, when-he-saw a house, beautiful, and to it (was) a vestibule, wide, lofty, and at the door servants, and command and prohibition.
sentences.i: As he was walking along some street he came upon a handsome house with a wide, lofty vestibule, and at its door stood servants and men of authority.
sentences.n: إِذْرَى is printed with the alif of raʾā missing (it should be إِذْ رَأَى “when he saw”), so there is no seat for the hamza; we point it as the letters stand and it reads idh-rā, with the hamza dropped. The same happens in مَارَى below. أَمْرٌ وَنَهْيٌ, “command and prohibition”, is a way of saying a household that gives orders.

sentences.t: فَسَأَلَ بَعْضَ مَنْ كَانَ وَاقِفًا هُنَاكَ فَقَالَ هِيَ لِإِنْسَانٍ مِنْ أَوْلَادِ الْبَرَامِكَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-saʾala baʿḍa man kāna wāqifan hunāka fa-qāla hiya li-insānin min awlādi al-barāmikati
sentences.l: So he asked some (one) of-whom was standing there; so he said, “It (is) for a man, of the children of the Barmakids.”
sentences.i: He asked one of those standing there, who said, “It belongs to a man of the Barmakid family.”
sentences.n: The Barmakids (al-Barāmika) were the great vizier family of the Abbasid court, proverbial for their generosity.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ أَخِي إِلَى الْبَوَّابِينَ وَسَاهُمْ شَيْئًا فَقَالُوا اُدْخُلْ بَابَ الدَّارِ تَجِدْ مَا تُحِبُّ مِنْ صَاحِبِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama akhī ilā al-bawwābīna wa-sāhum shayʾan fa-qālū udkhul bāba al-dāri tajid mā tuḥibbu min ṣāḥibinā
