sentences.l: So my brother advanced to the doorkeepers, and sāhum a thing; so they said, “Enter the door of the house, you will find what you love from our master.”
sentences.i: My brother went up to the doorkeepers and asked them for something. “Go in at the door of the house,” they said, “and you will find from our master what you wish.”
sentences.n: وَسَاهُمْ is printed so, with no lām. It is almost certainly وَسَأَلَهُمْ “and asked them”, and the translation takes it so; we do not alter the letters. تَجِدْ after the imperative is the jussive of a command followed by its result (“go in, you will find”).

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ الدِّهْلِيزَ وَمَشَى فِيهِ سَاعَةً فَوَصَلَ إِلَى دَارٍ فِي غَايَةِ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ الْمَلَاحَةِ وَالطُّرَفِ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala al-dihlīza wa-mashā fīhi sāʿatan fa-waṣala ilā dārin fī ghāyati mā yakūnu min al-malāḥati wa-al-ṭurafi
sentences.l: So he entered the vestibule, and walked in it an hour, so he arrived at a house, at the utmost of what can-be of the elegance and the rarities.
sentences.i: He entered the vestibule and walked through it for an hour, and so came to a house as elegant and rare as any could be.
sentences.n: الطُّرَفِ is pointed as “rarities, curiosities”; the stock pairing is الْمَلَاحَةِ وَالظَّرْفِ “grace and refinement” with ظ, so the printed ط may be a slip.

sentences.t: وَفِي وَسَطِهَا بُسْتَانٌ مَارَى مِثْلَهَا وَأَرْضُهَا مَفْرُوشَةٌ بِالرُّخَامِ وَسُتُورُهَا مُعَلَّقَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-fī wasaṭihā bustānun mā rā mithlahā wa-arḍuhā mafrūshatun bi-al-rukhāmi wa-sutūruhā muʿallaqatun
sentences.l: And in its middle (was) a garden, not he-saw its like; and its ground (was) spread with the marble, and its curtains (were) hung.
sentences.i: In the midst of it lay a garden the like of which one had never seen; its floor was spread with marble and its curtains were hung.
sentences.n: مَارَى stands for mā raʾā (see the note on إِذْرَى above): “[a garden] such that one had not seen its like”, a relative clause with no linking pronoun.

sentences.t: فَبَقِيَ أَخِي مُتَحَيِّرًا لَا يَدْرِي أَيْنَ يَتَّصِلُ فَمَضَى نَحْوَ صَدْرِ الْمَكَانِ فَرَأَى إِنْسَانًا حَسَنَ الْوَجْهِ وَاللِّحْيَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-baqiya akhī mutaḥayyiran lā yadrī ayna yattaṣilu fa-maḍā naḥwa ṣadri al-makāni fa-raʾā insānan ḥasana al-wajhi wa-al-liḥyati
sentences.l: So my brother remained bewildered, not knowing where he should join; so he went toward the upper-part of the place, so he saw a man, fair of the face and the beard.
sentences.i: My brother stood bewildered, not knowing where to turn, and then made his way toward the top of the hall, where he saw a man of fair face and handsome beard.
sentences.n: يَتَّصِلُ here means something like “to proceed, to make one’s way”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى أَخِي قَامَ لَهُ وَرَحَّبَ بِهِ وَسَأَلَهُ عَنْ حَالِهِ فَأَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّهُ مُحْتَاجٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā akhī qāma lahu wa-raḥḥaba bihi wa-saʾalahu ʿan ḥālihi fa-akhbarahu annahu muḥtājun
sentences.l: So when he saw my brother, he stood up for him, and welcomed him, and asked him about his state; so he informed him that he (was) needy.
sentences.i: When he saw my brother he rose to meet him, bade him welcome, and asked how he fared; and my brother told him that he was in want.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامَ أَخِي أَظْهَرَ لَهُ غَمًّا شَدِيدًا وَمَدَّيَدَهُ إِلَى ثِيَابِهِ فَخَرَقَهَا وَقَالَ أَكُونُ أَنَا بِبَلَدٍ وَأَنْتَ بِهَا جَائِعٌ لَاصَبْرَ لِي عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَوَعَدَهُ بِكُلِّ خَيْرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāma akhī aẓhara lahu ghamman shadīdan wa-madda yadahu ilā thiyābihi fa-kharaqahā wa-qāla akūnu anā bi-baladin wa-anta bihā jāʾiʿun lā ṣabra lī ʿalā dhālika wa-waʿadahu bi-kulli khayrin
sentences.l: So when he heard the speech of my brother, he showed him intense grief, and stretched his hand to his clothes and tore them, and said, “Shall I be in a town, and you in it hungry? No patience (is) to me for that.” And he promised him every good.
sentences.i: When he heard my brother’s words he showed deep distress; he put his hand to his clothes and tore them, crying, “Am I to be in a town where you are hungry? I cannot bear it!” And he promised him every good thing.
sentences.n: وَمَدَّيَدَهُ is printed as one word, wa-madda yadahu. أَكُونُ أَنَا بِبَلَدٍ is a question without a question-word, carried by the tone. Tearing one’s clothes is the conventional gesture of violent grief.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ لَا بُدَّ أَنْ تُمَاكِلَنِي فَقَالَ أَخِي يَا سَيِّدِي لَيْسَ لِي صَبْرٌ وَإِنِّي لَشَدِيدُ الْجُوعِ فَصَاحَ يَا غُلَامُ هَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu lā budda an tumākilanī fa-qāla akhī yā sayyidī laysa lī ṣabrun wa-innī la-shadīdu al-jūʿi fa-ṣāḥa yā ghulāmu hāti
sentences.l: So he said to him, “There is no escape that you eat-with-me.” So my brother said, “O my master, there is no patience to me, and indeed I am severe of the hunger.” So he cried, “O boy, bring!”
sentences.i: “You must eat with me,” he said. “My lord,” said my brother, “I have no patience left, for I am sorely hungry.” Then the host cried out, “Boy, bring —”
sentences.n: تُمَاكِلَنِي is the form mākala, “to eat together with”; the Classical verb is تُؤَاكِلَنِي with a hamza, which the edition does not write. The speech continues in the next sentence.

sentences.t: الطَّشْتَ وَالْإِ بْرِيقَ فَقَالَ لَهُ يَاضَيْفِي تَقَدَّمْ وَاغْسِلْ يَدَكَ
sentences.tr: al-ṭashta wa-al-i brīqa fa-qāla lahu yā ḍayfī taqaddam wa-ighsil yadaka
sentences.l: the-basin and-the-ewer; and-he-said to-him: 'O-my-guest, come-forward and-wash your-hand.'
sentences.i: ...the basin and the ewer. “My guest,” he said, “come forward and wash your hand.”
sentences.n: The sentence begins before this line: the verb governing the basin and ewer is in the previous sentence, so the accusative is our assumption. The print breaks إِبْرِيق with a stray space (والا بريق); we keep the two pieces as printed and read one word.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ أَخِي لِيَغْسِلَ يَدَهُ فَمَارٰى طَشْتًا وَلَابْرِيقًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma akhī li-yaghsila yadahu fa-mā rā ṭashtan wa-lā ibrīqan
sentences.l: So-rose my-brother to-wash his-hand, and-he-saw-not a-basin nor-an-ewer.
sentences.i: My brother rose to wash his hand, but he saw neither basin nor ewer.
sentences.n: رٰى is a defective spelling of رَأَى, marked with the dagger alif; Middle Arabic often leaves the hamza unwritten. In ولابريقا the two alifs of لَا + إِبْرِيق are written as one; read wa-lā ibrīqan.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَوْمَى كَأَنَّهُ يَغْسِلُ يَدَهُ ثُمَّ صَاحَ قَدِّمُوا الْمَائِدَةَ فَلَمْ يَرَأَخِي شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu awmā ka-annahu yaghsilu yadahu thumma ṣāḥa qaddimū al-māʾida fa-lam yara akhī shayʾan
sentences.l: Then indeed-he made-a-sign as-if-he washes his-hand; then he-cried: 'Bring the-table!' — and-not saw my-brother anything.
sentences.i: Then the man made a sign as though washing his own hand, and cried, “Bring the table!” — but my brother saw nothing.
sentences.n: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ 'then, behold, he...' is a stock narrative hinge; the inna only points at the subject. يَرَأَخِي is two words run together: يَرَ (jussive after لَمْ) + أَخِي.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِأَخِي تَفَضَّلْ كُلْ مِنْ هَذَا الطَّعَامِ وَلَا تَسْتَحِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-akhī tafaḍḍal kul min hādhā al-ṭaʿāmi wa-lā tastaḥī
sentences.l: Then he-said to-my-brother: 'Be-gracious, eat of this the-food, and-do-not you-are-shy.'
sentences.i: Then he said to my brother, “Pray be so kind: eat of this food, and do not be shy.”
sentences.n: وَلَا تَسْتَحِي keeps the final -ī after lā where Classical would have the jussive تَسْتَحِ. A Middle Arabic trait that recurs in this passage; vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: وَأَوْمَى بِيَدِهِ كَأَنَّهُ يَأْ كُلُ وَصَارَ الرَّجُلُ يَقُولُ لِأَخِي عَجَبًا لِقِلَّةِ أَكْلِكَ لَاتُقَصِّرْ فِى الْأَ كْلِ فَإِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْجُوعِ
sentences.tr: wa-awmā bi-yadihi ka-annahu yaʾ kulu wa-ṣāra al-rajulu yaqūlu li-akhī ʿajaban li-qillati aklika lā tuqaṣṣir fī al-a kli fa-innī aʿlamu mā anta ʿalayhi mina al-jūʿi
sentences.l: And-he-made-a-sign with-his-hand as-if-he eats; and-the-man began saying to-my-brother: 'A-wonder! at-the-scantiness of-your-eating! Do-not fall-short in the-eating, for-I know what you (are) upon-it of the-hunger.'
sentences.i: He gestured with his hand as though eating, and the man kept saying to my brother, “How strange, that you eat so little! Do not hold back from eating, for I know the hunger you are in.”
sentences.n: The print splits يَأْكُلُ and الأَكْل with a stray space (يا كل, الا كل); we keep the pieces as printed. صَارَ + imperfect: 'began to, kept on'.

sentences.t: فَجَعَلَ أَخِي يُومِي كَأَنَّهُ يَأْ كُلُ وَيَقُولُ لِأَخِي كُلْ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى حُسْنِ هَذَا الْخُبْزِ وَبَيَاضِهِ وَأَخِي لَايَرَى شَيْئًا
sentences.tr: fa-jaʿala akhī yūmī ka-annahu yaʾ kulu wa-yaqūlu li-akhī kul wa-unẓur ilā ḥusni hādhā al-khubzi wa-bayāḍihi wa-akhī lā yarā shayʾan
sentences.l: So my-brother set-about making-signs as-if-he eats, and-he-says to-my-brother: 'Eat, and-look at the-beauty of-this the-bread and-its-whiteness' — while my-brother sees-not anything.
sentences.i: So my brother began to make signs as though eating, while the host said to him, “Eat, and look at the beauty of this bread and its whiteness!” — and my brother saw nothing at all.
sentences.n: يُومِي is the Middle Arabic form of Classical يُومِئُ; compare أَوْمَى above.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ أَخِي قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ هَذَا رَجُلٌ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَهْزَؤُ بِالنَّاسِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna akhī qāla fī nafsihi hādhā rajulun yuḥibbu an yahzaʾu bi-al-nāsi
sentences.l: Then indeed my-brother said in his-self: 'This (is) a-man (who) loves that he-mocks at-the-people.'
sentences.i: Then my brother said to himself, “This man loves to make sport of people.”
sentences.n: يَهْزَؤُ is printed with ؤ and read yahzaʾu: the indicative where Classical would have the subjunctive يَهْزَأَ after أَنْ. Vocalised as spelled.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي يَا سَيِّدِي عُمْرِي مَا رَأَيْتُ أَحْسَنَ مِنْ بَيَاضِهِ وَلَا أَلَذَّمِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī yā sayyidī ʿumrī mā raʾaytu aḥsana min bayāḍihi wa-lā aladhdha minhu
sentences.l: So my-brother said to-him: 'O my-lord, my-lifetime — not I-saw finer than its-whiteness, nor more-delicious-than-it.'
sentences.i: “My lord,” said my brother, “never in my life have I seen anything finer than its whiteness, nor more delicious.”
sentences.n: عُمْرِي مَا رَأَيْتُ '(in) my lifetime I have not seen' is the colloquial idiom for 'never in my life', a Middle Arabic feature. ألذمنه is أَلَذَّ مِنْهُ ('more delicious than it') with the space lost in the print.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هَذَا خَبَزَتْهُ جَارِيَةٌ لِي اِشْتَرَيْتُهَا بِخَمْسِمِائَةِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla hādhā khabazathu jāriyatun lī ishtaraytuhā bi-khamsimiʾati dīnārin
sentences.l: He-said: 'This — baked-it a-girl of-mine; I-bought-her for five-hundred dinar.'
sentences.i: He said, “A slave-girl of mine baked it. I bought her for five hundred dinars.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَاحَ صَاحِبُ الدَّارِ يَا غُلَامُ قَدِّمِ الْهَرِيسَةَ أَوَّلَ الطَّعَامِ وَأَكْثِرْ عَلَيْهَا الدُّهْنَ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣāḥa ṣāḥibu al-dāri yā ghulāmu qaddimi al-harīsata awwala al-ṭaʿāmi wa-akthir ʿalayhā al-duhna
sentences.l: Then cried the-master of-the-house: 'O boy, present the-harisa first-of the-food, and-increase upon-it the-fat.'
sentences.i: Then the master of the house called out, “Boy! Bring the harīsa first of all the dishes, and put plenty of fat on it.”
sentences.n: Harīsa is a dish of pounded wheat and meat.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِأَخِي يَا ضَيْفِي بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ الطَّيِّبَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْهَرِيسَةِ فَبِحَيَاتِي كُلْ وَلَا تَسْتَحِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-akhī yā ḍayfī bi-Allāhi ʿalayka hal raʾayta al-ṭayyiba min hādhihi al-harīsati fa-bi-ḥayātī kul wa-lā tastaḥī
sentences.l: Then he-said to-my-brother: 'O my-guest, by-God upon-you, have-you-seen the-good than this the-harisa? By-my-life, eat, and-do-not be-shy.'
sentences.i: Then he said to my brother, “My guest, I adjure you by God: have you ever seen finer than this harīsa? By my life, eat, and do not be shy.”
sentences.n: الطَّيِّبَ is printed without the alif of the comparative; it is used as 'the better' (compare أَطْيَبَ later), so we read it that way.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا غُلَامُ قَدِّمْ لَنَا السِّكْبَاجَ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْقَطَا الْمُسَمَّنُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla yā ghulāmu qaddim lanā al-sikbāja alladhī fīhi al-qaṭā al-musammanu
sentences.l: Then he-said: 'O boy, present for-us the-sikbaj which in-it (is) the-sandgrouse, the-fattened.'
sentences.i: Then he said, “Boy! Bring us the sikbāj with the fattened sandgrouse in it.”
sentences.n: Sikbāj is meat stewed in vinegar.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِأَخِي قُمْ كُلْ يَا ضَيْفِي فَإِنَّكَ جَائِعٌ وَمُحْتَاجٌ لِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-akhī qum kul yā ḍayfī fa-innaka jāʾiʿun wa-muḥtājun li-dhālika
sentences.l: Then he-said to-my-brother: 'Rise, eat, O my-guest, for-you (are) hungry and-in-need of-that.'
sentences.i: Then he said to my brother, “Up, eat, my guest, for you are hungry and in need of it.”

sentences.t: فَصَارَ يَدُورُ حَنَكُهُ وَيَمْضَغُ وَأَقْبَلَ الرَّجُلُ يَسْتَدْعِي لَوْنًا بَعْدَ لَوْنٍ وَلَا يَحْضُرُ شَيْ إِلَّا هُوَ يَأْمُرُ أَخِي بِالْأَكْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāra yadūru ḥanakuhu wa-yamḍaghu wa-aqbala al-rajulu yastadʿī lawnan baʿda lawnin wa-lā yaḥḍuru shay illā huwa yaʾmuru akhī bi-al-akli
sentences.l: So his-jaw began-to turn, and-he-chewed; and-the-man went-on calling-for colour after colour, and-not is-brought a-thing except he orders my-brother to-the-eating.
sentences.i: So my brother set his jaw going round and chewed on nothing, while the man went on calling for dish after dish, and nothing was brought but he bade my brother eat of it.
sentences.n: لَوْن, 'colour', is the usual word for a kind of dish. شَيْ is the print's شي, short for شَيْء, vocalised as it stands.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَاحَ يَاغُلَامُ قَدِّمْ لَنَا الْفَرَارِيجَ الْمَحْشُوَّةَ بِالْفُسْتُقِ وَقَالَ لِأَخِي وَحَيَاتِكَ يَا ضَيْفِي هَذِهِ الْفَرَارِيجُ قَدْ سُمِّنَتْ بِالْفُسْتُقِ فَكُلْ مَالَا أَكَلْتُ مِثْلَهُ قَطُّ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣāḥa yā ghulāmu qaddim lanā al-farārīja al-maḥshūwata bi-al-fustuqi wa-qāla li-akhī wa-ḥayātika yā ḍayfī hādhihi al-farārīju qad summinat bi-al-fustuqi fa-kul mā lā akaltu mithlahu qaṭṭu
sentences.l: Then he-cried: 'O-boy, present for-us the-chickens, the-stuffed with-the-pistachio'; and-he-said to-my-brother: 'By-your-life, O my-guest, these the-chickens have-been-fattened with-the-pistachio; so eat — what-not I-ate its-like ever.'
sentences.i: Then he cried, “Boy! Bring us the chickens stuffed with pistachios,” and said to my brother, “By your life, my guest, these chickens have been fattened on pistachios, so eat — I have never eaten the like of them.”
sentences.n: مَالَا أَكَلْتُ مِثْلَهُ is printed with mā and lā joined; the sense is 'I have never eaten its like'. Classical would say مَا أَكَلْتُ or لَمْ آكُلْ; read it as a Middle Arabic negation.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي يَا سَيِّدِي هَذَا طَيِّبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī yā sayyidī hādhā ṭayyibun
sentences.l: So my-brother said to-him: 'O my-lord, this (is) good.'
sentences.i: My brother said to him, “My lord, this is delicious.”

sentences.t: وَأَقْبَلَ يُومِي بِيَدِهِ إِلَى فَمِ أَخِي كَأَنَّهُ يُلْقِمُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbala yūmī bi-yadihi ilā fami akhī ka-annahu yulqimuhu
sentences.l: And-he-turned, making-signs with-his-hand to the-mouth of-my-brother, as-if-he feeds-him-a-morsel.
sentences.i: Then he leaned forward, gesturing with his hand to my brother's mouth as though feeding him a morsel.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ يُعَدِّدُ هَذِهِ الْأَلْوَانَ وَيَصِفُهَا لِأَخِي وَهُوَ جَائِعٌ فَاشْتَدَّ جُوعُهُ وَهُوَ بِشَهْوَةِ رَغِيفِ شَعِيرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna yuʿaddidu hādhihi al-alwāna wa-yaṣifuhā li-akhī wa-huwa jāʾiʿun fa-ishtadda jūʿuhu wa-huwa bi-shahwati raghīfi shaʿīrin
sentences.l: And-he-was enumerating these the-colours and-describing-them to-my-brother, and-he (was) hungry, so-grew-fierce his-hunger, and-he in-craving of-a-loaf of-barley.
sentences.i: He went on naming these dishes and describing them to my brother, who was hungry; and the hunger grew fierce in him, till he longed for a loaf of barley bread.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ أَطْيَبَ مِنْ أَبَازِيرِ هَذِهِ الْأَ طْعِمَةِ فَقَالَ أَخِي لَا يَا سَيِّدِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu hal raʾayta aṭyaba min abāzīri hādhihi al-a ṭʿimati fa-qāla akhī lā yā sayyidī
sentences.l: Then he-said to-him: 'Have-you-seen better than the-spices of-these the-foods?' So my-brother said: 'No, O my-lord.'
sentences.i: Then he said to him, “Have you ever tasted better than the spices in these dishes?” “No, my lord,” said my brother.
sentences.n: الا طعمة is الأَطْعِمَة split by a stray space.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَوِّدِ الْأَكْلَ وَلَا تَسْتَحِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla jawwidi al-akla wa-lā tastaḥī
sentences.l: He-said: 'Do-well the-eating, and-do-not be-shy.'
sentences.i: He said, “Eat well, and do not be shy.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ قَدِ اكْتَفَيْتُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ فَصَاحَ الرَّجُلُ شِيلُوا هَذَا وَقَدِّمُوا الْحَلَاوَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla qadi iktafaytu mina al-ṭaʿāmi fa-ṣāḥa al-rajulu shīlū hādhā wa-qaddimū al-ḥalāwāti
sentences.l: He-said: 'I-have-had-enough of the-food.' So cried the-man: 'Take-away this, and-bring the-sweets!'
sentences.i: My brother said, “I have had enough of the food.” Then the man cried, “Take this away, and bring the sweets!”
sentences.n: شِيلُوا (from شَالَ, 'lift, carry off') is colloquial; it belongs to the speech of the street, not to the classical register.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ كُلْ مِنْ هَذَا فَإِنَّهُ جَيِّدٌ وَكُلْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَطَائِفِ بِحَيَاتِي خُذْ هَذِهِ الْقَطِيفَةَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ مِنْهَا الْجُلَّابُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu kul min hādhā fa-innahu jayyidun wa-kul min hādhihi al-qaṭāʾifi bi-ḥayātī khudh hādhihi al-qaṭīfata qabla an yanzila minhā al-jullābu
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him: 'Eat of this, for-it (is) fine; and-eat of these the-qatayif. By-my-life, take this the-qatifa before that-descends from-it the-julab.'
sentences.i: He said to him, “Eat of this, for it is fine; and eat of these pancakes — by my life, take this one before the syrup runs out of it.”
sentences.n: Qaṭāʾif are small pancakes soaked in syrup; julāb is rose-water syrup.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَخِي لَاعَلِمْتُكَ يَاسَيِّدِي وَأَقْبَلَ أَخِي يَسْأَلُهُ عَنْ كَثْرَةِ الْمِسْكِ الَّذِي فِي الْقَطَائِفِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla akhī lā ʿalimtuka yā sayyidī wa-aqbala akhī yasʾaluhu ʿan kathrati al-miski alladhī fī al-qaṭāʾifi
sentences.l: So my-brother said: 'No — I-have-not-known-you, O-my-lord'; and my-brother turned asking-him about the-abundance of-the-musk which (is) in the-qatayif.
sentences.i: My brother said, “No, my lord, I have never known your like,” and went on to ask him about the quantity of musk in the pancakes.
sentences.n: لَاعَلِمْتُكَ is obscure; we read it as an exclamation, 'I have not known (one like) you', but it may be corrupt.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هَذِهِ عَادَتِي يَصْنَعُونَ لِي فِي كُلِّ قَطِيفَةٍ مِثْقَالًا مِنَ الْمِسْكِ وَنِصْفَ مِثْقَالٍ مِنَ الْعَنْبَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla hādhihi ʿādatī yaṣnaʿūna lī fī kulli qaṭīfatin mithqālan mina al-miski wa-niṣfa mithqālin mina al-ʿanbari
sentences.l: He-said: 'This (is) my-habit: they-make for-me in every qatifa a-mithqal of the-musk and-half a-mithqal of the-ambergris.'
sentences.i: He said, “It is my custom. They put into every pancake for me a mithqāl of musk and half a mithqāl of ambergris.”
sentences.n: A mithqāl is a small weight, a few grams.

sentences.t: هَذَا كُلُّهُ وَأَخِي يُحَرِّكُ رَأْسَهُ وَفَمَهُ وَيَلْعَبُ بِأَشْدَاقِهِ
sentences.tr: hādhā kulluhu wa-akhī yuḥarriku raʾsahu wa-famahu wa-yalʿabu bi-ashdāqihi
sentences.l: This all-of-it — while my-brother moves his-head and-his-mouth and-plays with-his-jaws.
sentences.i: All this while my brother nodded his head, moved his mouth, and worked his jaws.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِأَخِي كُلْ مِنْ هَذَا اللَّوْزِ وَلَاتَسْتَحِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla li-akhī kul min hādhā al-lawzi wa-lā tastaḥī
sentences.l: So he-said to-my-brother: 'Eat of this the-almonds, and-do-not be-shy.'
sentences.i: Then he said to my brother, “Eat of these almonds, and do not be shy.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي يَاسَيِّدِي قَدِ اكْتَفَيْتُ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ لِي قُدْرَةٌ آكُلُ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī yā sayyidī qadi iktafaytu wa-lam yabqa lī qudratun ākulu shayʾan
sentences.l: So my-brother said to-him: 'O-my-lord, I-have-had-enough, and-there-remains not to-me power (that) I-eat anything.'
sentences.i: My brother said, “My lord, I have had enough, and I have no strength left to eat anything.”
sentences.n: قُدْرَةٌ آكُلُ 'power I eat' joins the two verbs without أَنْ, as in speech. شياً is printed with the tanwīn but without a seat for the hamza; read shayʾan.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا ضَيْفِي إِنْ أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَأْكُلَ وَتَتَفَرَّجَ فَاللَّهَ اللَّهَ لَاتَكُنْ جَائِعًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā ḍayfī in aradta an taʾkula wa-tatafarraja fa-Allāha Allāha lā takun jāʾiʿan
sentences.l: So he-said: 'O my-guest, if you-wished to-eat and-to-take-your-ease — God, God! do-not be hungry.'
sentences.i: Then he said, “My guest, if you want to eat and enjoy yourself, then for God's sake do not go hungry!”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَخِي يَا سَيِّدِي مَنْ يَأْ كُلُ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأَلْوَانِ كُلِّهَا كَيْفَ يَكُونُ جَائِعًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu akhī yā sayyidī man yaʾ kulu min hādhihi al-alwāni kullihā kayfa yakūnu jāʾiʿan
sentences.l: So my-brother said to-him: 'O my-lord, he-who eats of these the-colours all-of-them, how can-he-be hungry?'
sentences.i: My brother said, “My lord, how can anyone be hungry who eats of all these dishes?”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اِفْتَكَرَ أَخِي فِي نَفْسِهِ وَقَالَ لَأَعْمَلَنَّ عَمَلًا أُتَّوِّبُهُ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْفِعَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma iftakara akhī fī nafsihi wa-qāla la-aʿmalanna ʿamalan uttawwibuhu ʿan hādhihi al-fiʿāli
sentences.l: Then my-brother reflected in his-self and-said: 'Assuredly-I-shall-do a-deed (that) I-make-repent-him of these the-deeds.'
sentences.i: Then my brother thought to himself and said, “I will surely do something to make him repent of these doings.”
sentences.n: اتّوبه: the print puts a shadda on the tāʾ, which we keep. The sense seems to be أُتَوِّبُهُ, 'I shall make him repent', with the shadda misplaced; the form is uncertain.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ الرَّجُلُ قَدِّمُوا لَنَا الشَّرَابَ فَحَرَّكُوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِي الْهَوَاءِ حَتَّى كَأَنَّهُمْ قَدَّمُوا الشَّرَابَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla al-rajulu qaddimū lanā al-sharāba fa-ḥarrakū aydiyahum fī al-hawāʾi ḥattā ka-annahum qaddamū al-sharāba
sentences.l: Then said the-man: 'Present for-us the-drink.' So they-moved their-hands in the-air until as-if-they had-presented the-drink.
sentences.i: Then the man said, “Bring us the wine.” And they waved their hands in the air, as though they were serving it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَاوَلَهُ الْقَدَحَ وَقَالَ خُذْ هَذَا الْقَدَحَ فَإِنْ أَعْجَبَكَ فَعَرِّفْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma nāwalahu al-qadaḥa wa-qāla khudh hādhā al-qadaḥa fa-in aʿjabaka fa-ʿarrifnī
sentences.l: Then he-handed-him the-cup and-said: 'Take this the-cup; and-if it-pleases-you, then let-me-know.'
sentences.i: Then he handed him the cup, saying, “Take this cup, and if it pleases you, tell me.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي إِنَّهُ طَيِّبُ الرَّائِحَةِ لَكِنَّنِي تَعَوَّدْتُ بِشُرْبِ النَّبِيذِ الْعَتِيقِ الَّذِي لَهُ عِشْرُونَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī innahu ṭayyibu al-rāʾiḥati lākinnanī taʿawwadtu bi-shurbi al-nabīdhi al-ʿatīqi alladhī lahu ʿishrūna sanatan
sentences.l: So he-said to-him: 'O-my-lord, indeed-it (is) sweet of-the-scent, but-I have-become-used to-drinking the-wine, the-aged, which to-it (are) twenty years.'
sentences.i: He said, “My lord, its fragrance is sweet, but I am used to drinking old wine, old wine of twenty years.”
sentences.n: تَعَوَّدَ بِـ 'become used to' takes bi- in this text, where Classical has اعْتَادَ or تَعَوَّدَ + direct object.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ دُقْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-rajulu duq
sentences.l: So the-man said to-him: 'Taste!'
sentences.i: Then the man said to him, “Taste!”
sentences.n: دُقْ is ذُقْ ('taste') with د for ذ. The speech continues in the next sentence.

sentences.t: هَذَا الْبَابُ فَإِنَّكَ لَا تَقْدِرُ تَشْرَبُ مِنْهُ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: hādhā al-bābu fa-innaka lā taqdiru tashrabu minhu shayʾan
sentences.l: This the-door; for indeed-you, not you-are-able (to) you-drink from-it anything.
sentences.i: This is the way of it: you cannot drink anything of it.
sentences.n: The host's speech continues from the previous sentence, so what الباب (bāb, ‘door’, here perhaps ‘the matter, the case’) points to is not visible here. لَا تَقْدِرُ تَشْرَبُ puts two imperfects side by side with no أَنْ between them, a Middle Arabic habit you will meet constantly; read it as ‘you cannot drink’.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي مِنْ إِحْسَانِكَ وَأَوْمَى أَخِي بِيَدِهِ كَأَنَّهُ بِشَرْبِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ هَنِيئًا وَصِحَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī min iḥsānika wa-awmā akhī bi-yadihi ka-annahu bi-sharbihi fa-qāla lahu hanīʾan wa-ṣiḥḥatan
sentences.l: So he-said: “O my-lord, (it is) of your-benevolence.” And my-brother gestured with-his-hand as-if-he (were) at-the-drinking-of-it. So he-said to-him: “Wholesome, and health.”
sentences.i: He said, “My lord, it is of your kindness.” And my brother made a sign with his hand, as though he were drinking. Then the host said to him, “May it sit well with you, and good health.”
sentences.n: كَأَنَّهُ بِشَرْبِهِ is read here as ‘as though at the drinking of it’; it may be a slip or an Egyptian b- spelling for يشربه ‘as though he were drinking it’. The sense is the same either way: the two men are miming. أَوْمَى is a by-form of أَوْمَأَ ‘to signal, motion’. هَنِيئًا is the stock wish said to someone drinking.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ صَاحِبَ الْبَيْتِ أَوْمَى وَشَرِبَ ثُمَّ نَاوَلَ أَخِي قَدَحًا ثَانِيًا فَشَرِبَهُ وَأَظْهَرَ أَنَّهُ سَكِرَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna ṣāḥiba al-bayti awmā wa-shariba thumma nāwala akhī qadaḥan thāniyan fa-sharibahu wa-aẓhara annahu sakira
sentences.l: Then indeed (the) owner-of the-house gestured and drank; then he-handed my-brother a-cup, a-second; so-he-drank-it and showed that-he (had) become-drunk.
sentences.i: Then the master of the house made a sign and drank, and handed my brother a second cup, which he drank, and he made a show of being drunk.
sentences.n: أَظْهَرَ أَنَّهُ سَكِرَ, ‘he showed that he was drunk’: the drunkenness is an act, like the cups.

sentences.t: وَغَافَلَهُ أَخِي وَرَفَعَ يَدَهُ حَتَّى بَانَ بَيَاضُ إِبْطِهِ وَصَفَعَهُ فِى رَقَبَتِهِ صَفْعَةً رَنَّ لَهَا الْمَكَانُ ثُمَّ ثَنَّى عَلَيْهِ بِصَفْعَةٍ ثَانِيَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ghāfalahu akhī wa-rafaʿa yadahu ḥattā bāna bayāḍu ibṭihi wa-ṣafaʿahu fī raqabatihi ṣafʿatan ranna lahā al-makānu thumma thannā ʿalayhi bi-ṣafʿatin thāniyatin
sentences.l: And my-brother took-him-off-guard, and raised his-hand until the-whiteness-of his-armpit appeared, and slapped-him on his-neck, a-slap the-place rang at-it; then he-doubled upon-him with-a-slap, a-second.
sentences.i: My brother caught him off his guard, raised his hand so high that the whiteness of his armpit showed, and struck him on the nape of the neck with a blow that made the whole place ring. Then he followed it up with a second.
sentences.n: ثَنَّى عَلَيْهِ بِـ is ‘to follow up on him with’, to repeat a blow; the edition itself prints the shadda on ثنّى, and it is kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ الرَّجُلُ مَا هَذَا يَا سِفْلَةُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla al-rajulu mā hādhā yā siflatu
sentences.l: Then said the-man: “What (is) this, O base-fellow?”
sentences.i: Then the man said, “What is this, you wretch?”
sentences.n: سِفْلَة is a low fellow, one of the rabble, used here as an insult to one man.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِى عَبْدُكَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ وَأَدْخَلْتَهُ مَنْزِلَكَ وَأَطْعَمْتَهُ الزَّادَ وَأَسْقَيْتَهُ الْخَمْرَ الْعَتِيقَ فَسَكِرَ وَعَرْبَدَ عَلَيْكَ وَأَنْتَ أَعْلَا مَنْ حَمَلَ جَهْلَهُ وَعَفْوَذَنْبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī ʿabduka anʿamta ʿalayhi wa-adkhaltahu manzilaka wa-aṭʿamtahu al-zāda wa-asqaytahu al-khamra al-ʿatīqa fa-sakira wa-ʿarbada ʿalayka wa-anta aʿlā man ḥamala jahlahu wa-ʿafwa dhanbihi
sentences.l: So he-said: “O my-lord, your-servant — you-showed-favour upon-him, and-you-brought-him-in (to) your-house, and-you-fed-him the-provisions, and-you-gave-him-to-drink the-wine, the-aged; so he-became-drunk and-was-riotous against-you; and you (are) loftier (than) whoever bore his-folly and the-pardoning-of his-offence.”
sentences.i: He said, “My lord, here is your servant: you showed him favour, took him into your house, fed him from your table and gave him your old wine to drink, and he grew drunk and unruly with you. But you are loftier than any who bear with a man’s folly and pardon his fault.”
sentences.n: أَعْلَا is printed with a final alif where Classical writes أَعْلَى; this is the edition’s spelling, kept. وَعَفْوَذَنْبِهِ is printed as one word; it is read as وَعَفْوَ ذَنْبِهِ ‘and the pardoning of his offence’, a second object of حَمَلَ. If you would rather take عَفَوْ as a verb ‘and pardoned’, the sense hardly changes. عَرْبَدَ means to turn riotous or quarrelsome in drink.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامَ أَخِي ضَحِكَ ضَحِكًا عَالِيًا ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ لِي زَمَانًا طَوِيلًا أَسْخَرُ بِالنَّاسِ وَأَتَمَاجَنُ عَلَى الْأَصْحَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāma akhī ḍaḥika ḍaḥikan ʿāliyan thumma qāla lahu inna lī zamānan ṭawīlan askharu bi-al-nāsi wa-atamājanu ʿalā al-aṣḥābi
sentences.l: And when he-heard (the) speech-of my-brother he-laughed a-laughing, loud; then he-said to-him: “Indeed, to-me (is) a-time, long — I-mock at-the-people and-I-play-the-buffoon upon the-companions.”
sentences.i: When he heard my brother’s words he burst into loud laughter, and said to him, “For a long while now I have been making sport of people and playing the jester with my companions,
sentences.n: إِنَّ لِي زَمَانًا طَوِيلًا أَسْخَرُ: ‘I have a long time (that) I mock’, meaning ‘for a long time I have been mocking’; the present verb simply follows the time-phrase. سَخِرَ بِـ is ‘to mock at’.

sentences.t: فَمَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْهُمْ مَنْ لَهُ طَاقَةٌ وَفِطْنَةٌ دَخَلَ مَعِي فِي جَمِيعِ أُمُورِي غَيْرَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-mā raʾaytu minhum man lahu ṭāqatun wa-fiṭnatun dakhala maʿī fī jamīʿi umūrī ghayraka
sentences.l: And-not I-saw among-them (any) who has capacity and sharpness (who) entered with-me in all (of) my-affairs, other-than-you.
sentences.i: and among them all I have never found one with the strength and wit to enter with me into all my affairs — none but you.
sentences.n: The relative clauses are strung together with no linking word: ‘one who has capacity and wit, (who) entered with me…’. The quotation continues from the previous sentence.

sentences.t: وَالْآنَ فَقَدْ عَفَوْتُ عَنْكَ فَكُنْ نَدِيمِي عَلَى الْحَقِيقَةِ وَلَا تُفَارِقْنِي أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: wa-al-āna fa-qad ʿafawtu ʿanka fa-kun nadīmī ʿalā al-ḥaqīqati wa-lā tufāriqnī abadan
sentences.l: And now, I-have-indeed pardoned from-you; so be my-boon-companion upon the-truth, and not you-part-from-me ever.
sentences.i: And now I have pardoned you. Be my boon-companion in earnest, and never leave me.
sentences.n: عَلَى الْحَقِيقَةِ ‘in truth, truly’. A نَدِيم is a companion in drink and talk.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِإِخْرَاجِ عِدَّةِ أَلْوَانِ الطَّعَامِ الْمَذْكُورَةِ أَوَّلًا
sentences.tr: thumma amara bi-ikhrāji ʿiddati alwāni al-ṭaʿāmi al-madhkūrati awwalan
sentences.l: Then he-commanded the-bringing-out-of a-number-of kinds-of the-food, the-mentioned, first.
sentences.i: Then he ordered that the various dishes named at the outset be brought out.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلَ هُوَ وَأَخِي حَتَّى اكْتَفَيَا ثُمَّ انْتَقَلَا إِلَى مَجْلِسِ الشَّرَابِ فَإِذَا فِيهِ جَوَارِي كَأَنَّهُنَّ الْأَقْمَارُ فَغَنَّيْنَ بِجَمِيعِ الْأَلْحَانِ وَجَمِيعِ الْمَلَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-akala huwa wa-akhī ḥattā iktafayā thumma intaqalā ilā majlisi al-sharābi fa-idhā fīhi jawārī ka-annahunna al-aqmāru fa-ghannayna bi-jamīʿi al-alḥāni wa-jamīʿi al-malāhī
sentences.l: And-he-ate, he and-my-brother, until the-two-were-satisfied; then the-two-moved to the-sitting-room-of the-drink; and-behold in-it (were) slave-girls, as-if-they (were) the-moons; and-they-sang with-all the-melodies and all the-instruments-of-diversion.
sentences.i: He and my brother ate until they were satisfied, and then moved to the drinking-room, where they found slave-girls like moons, who sang every kind of air to every kind of instrument.
sentences.n: جَوَارِي is printed with a final yā; Classical has the tanwīn form جَوَارٍ ‘slave-girls’ (plural of جَارِيَة). It is vocalised as printed. فَإِذَا فِيهِ is ‘and lo, in it (were)…’. Plain hearing of the sentence: the girls are the music-makers; the أُنْس of the room lies in them.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَا وَشَرِبَا حَتَّى غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِمَا السُّكْرُ وَاسْتَأْنَسَ الرَّجُلُ بِأَخِي حَتَّى صَارَ كَأَنَّهُ أَخُوهُ وَأَحَبَّهُ مَحَبَّةً عَظِيمَةً وَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāmā wa-sharibā ḥattā ghalaba ʿalayhimā al-sukru wa-istaʾnasa al-rajulu bi-akhī ḥattā ṣāra ka-annahu akhūhu wa-aḥabbahu maḥabbatan ʿaẓīmatan wa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then the-two-rose and-drank until drunkenness overcame them-both; and the-man grew-at-ease with-my-brother until he-became as-if-he (were) his-brother, and-loved-him a-love, great, and-bestowed-a-robe upon-him.
sentences.i: Then the two of them rose and drank until drink overcame them both. The man grew so easy in my brother’s company that he came to treat him as a brother, loved him dearly, and gave him a robe of honour.
sentences.n: خَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ, literally ‘he cast off (his garment) upon him’, is the standard phrase for bestowing a robe of honour.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ عَادَا لِمَا كَانَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْأَكْلِ وَالشُّرْبِ وَلَمْ يَزَالَا كَذَلِكَ مُدَّةَ عِشْرِينَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu ʿādā li-mā kānā ʿalayhi min al-akli wa-al-shurbi wa-lam yazālā kadhālika muddata ʿishrīna sanatan
sentences.l: And when the-morning morned, the-two-returned to-what the-two-were upon, of the-eating and the-drinking; and not the-two-ceased thus (for) a-span-of twenty year.
sentences.i: When morning came they went back to the eating and drinking they had been at, and so they continued for twenty years.
sentences.n: أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ, ‘the morning became morning’, is simply ‘day broke’. عَادَ لِـ is ‘to go back to’; كَانَ عَلَى is ‘to be engaged in’.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ مَاتَ وَقَبَضَ السُّلْطَانُ عَلَي مَا لَهُ وَمَا احْتَوَى عَلَيْهِ أَخِي وَصَادَرَهُ السُّلْطَانُ حَتَّى خَلَّاهُ فَقِيرًا لَايَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-rajula māta wa-qabaḍa al-sulṭānu ʿalā mā lahu wa-mā iḥtawā ʿalayhi akhī wa-ṣādarahu al-sulṭānu ḥattā khallāhu faqīran lā yaqdiru ʿalā shayʾin
sentences.l: Then indeed the-man died, and the-sultan seized upon what (was) his and what my-brother comprised upon-it; and the-sultan confiscated-from-him until he-left-him poor, not-able upon anything.
sentences.i: Then the man died, and the sultan laid hold of his estate and of whatever my brother held, and stripped him of it until he left him a pauper, unable to do anything.
sentences.n: عَلَي is printed with a yā for عَلَى, and kept; read ʿalā. لَايَقْدِرُ is printed as one word, ‘(he is) not able’. صَادَرَ is to confiscate, to strip a man of his goods.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ أَخِي هَارِبًا عَلَي وَجْهِهِ فَلَمَّا تَوَسَّطَ الطَّرِيقَ خَرَجَ عَلَيْهِ الْعَرَبُ فَأَسَرُوهُ وَأَتَوْابِهِ إِلَى حَيِّهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja akhī hāriban ʿalā wajhihi fa-lammā tawassaṭa al-ṭarīqa kharaja ʿalayhi al-ʿarabu fa-asarūhu wa-atawā bihi ilā ḥayyihim
sentences.l: And my-brother went-out fleeing upon his-face; and when he-reached-the-middle-of the-road, the-Arabs came-out upon-him, and-took-him-captive, and-brought-him to their-encampment.
sentences.i: So my brother fled, going wherever his face led him. When he was halfway along the road, Bedouin came out against him, took him captive, and brought him to their camp.
sentences.n: عَلَى وَجْهِهِ, ‘on his face’, means aimlessly, whichever way he happened to face. وَأَتَوْابِهِ is printed as one word: وَأَتَوْا بِهِ ‘and they brought him’ (أَتَى بِـ is ‘to bring’). الْعَرَبُ here are the desert Arabs, Bedouin.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ الَّذِى أَسَرَهُ يُعَذِّبُهُ وَيَقُولُ لَهُ اشْتَرِ رُوحَكَ مِنِّي بِالْأَمْوَالِ وَإِلَّاقَتَلْتُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra alladhī asarahu yuʿadhdhibuhu wa-yaqūlu lahu ishtari rūḥaka minnī bi-al-amwāli wa-illā qataltuka
sentences.l: And the-one-who took-him-captive began (to) torture-him and-say to-him: “Buy your-soul from-me with-the-riches, or-else I-killed-you.”
sentences.i: And his captor took to tormenting him, saying, “Buy your life back from me with money, or I will kill you.”
sentences.n: وَإِلَّاقَتَلْتُكَ is printed as one word, وَإِلَّا قَتَلْتُكَ ‘and if not, I (will) kill you’; the perfect قَتَلْتُ stands for a threatened future. اشْتَرِ رُوحَكَ is ‘ransom yourself’.

sentences.t: فَجَعَلَ أَخِي يَبْكِى وَيَقُولُ وَاللَّهِ لَا أَمْلِكُ شَيْئًا وَأَنَا أَسِيرُكَ فَافْعَلْ مَا شِئْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-jaʿala akhī yabkī wa-yaqūlu wa-Allāhi lā amliku shayʾan wa-anā asīruka fa-afʿal mā shiʾta
sentences.l: And my-brother began (to) weep and-say: “By-God, not I-own anything, and-I (am) your-captive — so do what you-wished.”
sentences.i: My brother began to weep, saying, “By God, I own nothing, and I am your captive; do as you please.”
sentences.n: جَعَلَ plus an imperfect means ‘began to’. فَافْعَلْ مَا شِئْتَ, ‘do what you have wished’, is ‘do as you will’.

sentences.t: فَأَخْرَجَ الْبَدَوِيُّ سِكِّينًا وَ قَطَعَ شَفَتَيْ أَخِي وَشَدَّدَ عَايْهِ فِى الْمَطَابِخِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhraja al-badawiyyu sikkīnan wa-qaṭaʿa shafatay akhī wa-shaddada ʿalayhi fī al-maṭābikhi
sentences.l: And the-Bedouin took-out a-knife and — cut (the) two-lips-of my-brother, and was-severe upon-him in the-kitchens.
sentences.i: Then the Bedouin drew a knife and cut off both my brother’s lips, and dealt harshly with him in the kitchens.
sentences.n: The print leaves a lone و at the end of its line, with قطع opening the next: kept as its own word, read as ‘and’. عَايْهِ is evidently a misprint for عَلَيْهِ ‘upon him’; it is vocalised as printed and transliterated as the word is meant. The Bedouin’s ‘kitchens’ (مَطَابِخ, plural of مَطْبَخ) are where he is put to work.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ لَهُ زَوْجَةٌ حَسْنَاءُ وَكَانَتْ إِذَا خَرَجَ الْبَدَوِيُّ تَتَعَرَّضُ لِأَخِي وَتُرَا وِدُهُ وَهُوَ يَمْتَنِعُ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna lahu zawjatun ḥasnāʾu wa-kānat idhā kharaja al-badawiyyu tataʿarraḍu li-akhī wa-turāwiduhu wa-huwa yamtaniʿu minhā
sentences.l: And there-was to-him a-wife, beautiful; and she-was, when the-Bedouin went-out, presenting-herself to-my-brother and soliciting-him, while-he refrained from-her.
sentences.i: The Bedouin had a beautiful wife, who, whenever he went out, made advances to my brother and tried to seduce him, while he held back from her.
sentences.n: كَانَتْ إِذَا خَرَجَ … تَتَعَرَّضُ: كَانَ with an imperfect is the habitual ‘she used to’. تُرَا وِدُهُ is one word, تُرَاوِدُهُ ‘she solicits him’, split by a space in the print; each half is vocalised as it stands.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ رَاوَدَتْ أَخِي فَقَامَ وَلَا عَبَهَا وَأَجْلَسَهَا فِي حُجْرَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna yawman min al-ayyāmi rāwadat akhī fa-qāma wa-lāʿabahā wa-ajlasahā fī ḥujratin
sentences.l: And when it-was a-day of the-days, she-solicited my-brother; so he-rose and-toyed-with-her and-seated-her in a-chamber.
sentences.i: One day she made advances to my brother again, and this time he rose, toyed with her, and sat her down in a chamber.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّا كَانَ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ is the stock ‘one day’. وَلَا عَبَهَا is one word split by a space, وَلَاعَبَهَا ‘and he toyed with her’ (لَاعَبَ, to play with, to dally with). The phrase ‘this time’ in the idiomatic line is the reader’s inference from the preceding sentence; the Arabic says only ‘one day’.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَكَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِزَوْجِهَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa kadhālika wa-idhā bi-zawjihā dakhala ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And while he (was) thus — and-behold, with-her-husband, he-entered upon-her.
sentences.i: While he was so engaged, behold, her husband came in upon her.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِزَوْجِهَا: the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears, ‘and behold, her husband’. هُوَكَذَلِكَ is printed as one word, ‘he (being) thus’.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَى أَخِي قَالَ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ يَا مَلْعُونُ آلَانَ تُرِيدُ تُفْسِدُ عَلَيَّ زَوْجَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ilā akhī qāla lahu waylaka yā malʿūnu ālāna turīdu tufsidu ʿalayya zawjatī
sentences.l: And when he-looked at my-brother he-said to-him: “Woe-to-you! O accursed-one! Now? You-want (to) ruin upon-me my-wife?”
sentences.i: When he saw my brother he said to him, “Woe to you, accursed wretch! Now you would corrupt my wife against me?”
sentences.n: آلَانَ is أَ ‘is it that…?’ fused with الآن ‘now’, so the sentence is a question; the edition prints it with آ. تُرِيدُ تُفْسِدُ again sets two imperfects side by side. The edition prints the shadda on عليّ, and it is kept.

sentences.t: وَأَخْرَجَ سِكِّينًا وَقَطَعَ ذَكَرَهُ وَحَمَلَهُ عَلَى جَمَلٍ وَطَرَدَهُ فَوْقَ جَبَلٍ وَتَرَكَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-akhraja sikkīnan wa-qaṭaʿa dhakarahu wa-ḥamalahu ʿalā jamalin wa-ṭaradahu fawqa jabalin wa-tarakahu
sentences.l: And he-took-out a-knife and cut-off his-penis, and-loaded-him upon a-camel and-drove-him-away above a-mountain, and-left-him.
sentences.i: He drew a knife and cut off his member, then set him on a camel, drove him out onto a mountain, and left him there.

sentences.t: فَجَازَ عَلَيْهِ الْمُسَافِرُونَ فَعَرَفُوهُ فَأَطْعَمُوهُ وَأَسْقَوْهُ وَأَعْلَمُونِي بِخَبَرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-jāza ʿalayhi al-musāfirūna fa-ʿarafūhu fa-aṭʿamūhu wa-asqawhu wa-aʿlamūnī bi-khabarihi
sentences.l: And the-travellers passed upon-him, and-recognised-him, and-fed-him and-gave-him-to-drink, and-informed-me of-his-news.
sentences.i: Travellers passing that way came upon him and knew him; they fed him and gave him drink, and sent me word of his plight.
sentences.n: جَازَ عَلَيْهِ is ‘passed by him’; أَعْلَمَ بِـ is ‘to inform of’. The narrator is the barber, telling the Caliph of his brother.

sentences.t: فَجِئْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَحَمَلْتُهُ وَدَخَلْتُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ وَرَتَّبْتُ لَهُ مَا يَكْفِيهِ وَهَا أَنَا جِئْتُ عِنْدَكَ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَخِفْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-jiʾtu ilayhi wa-ḥamaltuhu wa-dakhaltu bi-al-madīnati wa-rattabtu lahu mā yakfīhi wa-hā anā jiʾtu ʿindaka yā amīra al-muʾminīna wa-khiftu
sentences.l: And I-came to-him and-carried-him and-entered with-the-city, and-arranged for-him what suffices-him; and-lo, I (have) come at-you, O commander-of the-believers, and-I-feared —
sentences.i: So I went to him, took him up, and entered the city with him, and arranged for him all that he needed. And now I have come to you, Commander of the Faithful, and I was afraid —
sentences.n: دَخَلْتُ بِالْمَدِينَةِ uses بِـ with the place entered, as Middle Arabic does; ‘with him’ is understood. جِئْتُ عِنْدَكَ, ‘I came at you’, uses عِنْدَ where Classical wants إِلَى. The sentence continues in the next.

sentences.t: أَنْ أَرْجِعَ قَبْلَ إِخْبَارِكَ فَيَكُونُ ذَلِكَ غَلَطًا وَرَائِي سِتَّةُ إِخْوَةٍ وَأَنَا أَقُومُ بِهِمْ
sentences.tr: an arjiʿa qabla ikhbārika fa-yakūnu dhālika ghalaṭan wa-warāʾī sittatu ikhwatin wa-anā aqūmu bihim
sentences.l: that I return before your-informing, so that-is a mistake; and behind-me (are) six brothers, and I stand with-them.
sentences.i: For me to go back before telling you would be a mistake: I have six brothers behind me, and I am their support.
sentences.n: The sentence begins in the previous one; the barber is excusing himself, and the main clause is cut off at the edge. أَقُومُ بِـ is “I see to, provide for”. After فَـ the verb is vocalised as the indicative (فَيَكُونُ), as it reads in the spoken register; Classical would be the subjunctive.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ أَمِيرُالْمُؤْمِنِينَ قِصَّتِي وَمَا أَخْبَرْتُ بِهِ عَنْ إِخْوَتِي ضَحِكَ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa amīru al-muʾminīna qiṣṣatī wa-mā akhbartu bihi ʿan ikhwatī ḍaḥika wa-qāla
sentences.l: So when the-commander-of-the-believers heard my-story and what I-informed with-it about my-brothers, he-laughed and said:
sentences.i: When the Commander of the Faithful had heard my story, and what I had told of my brothers, he laughed and said:
sentences.n: The edition prints أمير المؤمنين (the caliph’s title) as a single word, with no space; it is kept so.

sentences.t: صَدَقْتَ يَا صَامِتُ أَنْتَ قَلِيلُ الْكَلَامِ مَا عِنْدَكَ فُضُولٌ وَلَكِنِ الْآنَ اُخْرُجْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْبَلْدَةِ وَاسْكُنْ غَيْرَهَا
sentences.tr: ṣadaqta yā ṣāmitu anta qalīlu al-kalāmi mā ʿindaka fuḍūlun wa-lākini al-āna ukhruj min hādhihi al-baldati wa-uskun ghayrahā
sentences.l: You-spoke-truly, O Silent-one! You (are) little-of the-speech; there-is-not with-you meddling. But now, go-out from this the-town and dwell (in) other-than-it.
sentences.i: You have spoken truly, O Silent One: you are sparing of speech, and there is no meddling in you. But now, leave this town and settle elsewhere.
sentences.n: Ṣāmit, “Silent”, is the name the barber gives himself in his tale; the caliph uses it here, and the irony (the barber has just talked at length) is plain from what follows: banishment. فُضُول (“meddling, officiousness”) is the barber’s great theme.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَفَانِي بِالتَّرْسِيمِ عَلَيَّ حَتَّى دَخَلْتُ الْبِلَادَ وَطُفْتُ الْأَقَالِيمَ أَيْ أَنْ سَمِعْتُ بِمَوْتِهِ وَخِلَافَةِ غَيْرِهِ أَتَيْتُ الْمَدِينَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma nafānī bi-al-tarsīmi ʿalayya ḥattā dakhaltu al-bilāda wa-ṭuftu al-aqālīma ayy an samiʿtu bi-mawtihi wa-khilāfati ghayrihi ataytu al-madīnata
sentences.l: Then he-banished-me with-the-tarsīm upon-me until I-entered the-lands and circled the-regions, that-is, (until) I-heard of-his-death and the-caliphate of-another, (and) I-came (to) the-city.
sentences.i: Then he banished me by an order laid upon me, and I passed through land after land and went about the regions, until I heard of his death and of another’s succession to the caliphate, and came back to the city.
sentences.n: التَّرْسِيم (tarsīm) is an administrative order, in later Egyptian usage one restricting a person’s movements; here it evidently means an order of exile, but the sense is not certain. أَيْ أَنْ سَمِعْتُ is elliptical: “that is, [until] I heard”. أَتَيْتُ الْمَدِينَةَ takes the place directly, without إِلَى.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْتُ إِخْوَتِي قَدْ مَاتُوا وَوَقَعْتُ عِنْدَ هَذَا الشَّابِّ وَفَعَلْتُ مَعَهُ أَحْسَنَ الْفِعَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadtu ikhwatī qad mātū wa-waqaʿtu ʿinda hādhā al-shābbi wa-faʿaltu maʿahu aḥsana al-fiʿāli
sentences.l: So I-found my-brothers (that) they-had died, and I-fell at this the-youth, and I-did with-him the-best (of) the-deeds.
sentences.i: I found my brothers dead, and I came to rest with this young man, and did him every kindness.
sentences.n: وَقَعَ عِنْدَ: “to land up with, fall in with”, here with a sense of settling in his company.

sentences.t: وَلَوْلَا أَنَالَقُتِلَ وَقَدِ اتَّهَمَنِي بِشَيْءٍ مَاهُوَ فِيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-lawlā anā la-quṭila wa-qadi ittahamanī bi-shayʾin mā huwa fiyya
sentences.l: And had-it-not-been (for) me, he-would-have-been-killed; and he-had accused-me with-a-thing (that) is-not in me.
sentences.i: Had it not been for me, he would have been killed; and yet he has accused me of something that is not in me.
sentences.n: The edition prints أنا لقتل run together as one word. We read it as أَنَا لَقُتِلَ, “were it not for me he would have been killed”, which fits the sense; the person who would have been killed (surely the young man) is not named. The final فِيَّ is spelled في, and the sentence ends there. ماهو is likewise printed as a single word.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا يَا جَمَاعَةُ مَا نُقِلَ عَنِّي مِنَ الْفُضُولِ بَاطِلٌ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā yā jamāʿatu mā nuqila ʿannī min al-fuḍūli bāṭilun
sentences.l: And this, O company, what was-transmitted about-me of the-meddling (is) false.
sentences.i: And what is reported of me, my friends, about meddling is false.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا لِأَجْلِ هَذَا الشَّابِّ طُفْتُ بُلْدَ انًا كَثِيرْ حَتَّى وَصَلْتُ إِلَى هَذِهِ الْأَرْضِ وَحَصَّلْتُهُ عِنْدَكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-anā li-ajli hādhā al-shābbi ṭuftu buldānan kathīr ḥattā waṣaltu ilā hādhihi al-arḍi wa-ḥaṣṣaltuhu ʿindakum
sentences.l: And I, for-the-sake-of this the-youth, circled lands many, until I-arrived at this the-land, and obtained-him with-you.
sentences.i: It was for this young man’s sake that I wandered through many lands, until I reached this country and found him here among you.
sentences.n: The print has a space inside the word: بلد انا is بُلْدَانًا, “lands”, split in two; we point the two halves so that they read together. كَثِيرْ is the edition’s masculine singular adjective with a plural noun (Classical: كَثِيرَةً); we leave the ending unmarked as it stands.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا يَا جَمَاعَةَ الْخَيْرِ مَاهُوَ مِنْ مُرُوَّتِي
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā yā jamāʿata al-khayri mā huwa min muruwwatī
sentences.l: So this, O company of-the-good, (is) not of my-manliness.
sentences.i: So this, good people, is no part of my manly honour.
sentences.n: مُرُوَّة (muruwwa) is manly virtue, the code of honour of a decent man. ماهو is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَيَّاطُ لِمَلِكِ الصِّينِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khayyāṭu li-maliki al-ṣīni
sentences.l: So the-tailor said to-the-king (of) China:
sentences.i: The tailor went on, speaking to the King of China:

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْنَا قِصَّةَ الْمُزَيِّنِ وَكَثْرَةَ كَلَامِهِ وَأَنَّ الْمُزَيِّنَ ظَلَمَ مَعَ هَذَا الشَّابِّ أَخَذْنَا الْمُزَيِّنَ وَقَبَضْنَا عَلَيْهِ وَحَبَسْنَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿnā qiṣṣata al-muzayyini wa-kathrata kalāmihi wa-anna al-muzayyina ẓalama maʿa hādhā al-shābbi akhadhnā al-muzayyina wa-qabaḍnā ʿalayhi wa-ḥabasnāhu
sentences.l: So when we-heard the-barber’s story and the-abundance (of) his-speech, and that the-barber had-wronged with this the-youth, we-took the-barber and seized upon-him and imprisoned-him.
sentences.i: When we had heard the barber’s story, and how much he talked, and that the barber had dealt unjustly with this young man, we took hold of him, seized him, and shut him up.
sentences.n: We read ظَلَمَ as active (“he did wrong”), since the company then seizes the barber; ظَلَمَ مَعَ, “wronged in dealings with”, takes the place of the Classical direct object.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْنَا نَحْنُ آمِنِينَ فَأَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا وَتَمَّتِ الْوَلِيمَةُ إِلَى أَنْ أَذَّنَ الْعَصْرُ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasnā naḥnu āminīna fa-akalnā wa-sharibnā wa-tammati al-walīmatu ilā an adhdhana al-ʿaṣru
sentences.l: And we-sat, we, secure; so we-ate and we-drank, and the-feast was-completed, until the-afternoon called (the call).
sentences.i: And we sat at our ease, free of fear, and ate and drank, and the feast ran its course until the call to the afternoon prayer.
sentences.n: أَذَّنَ الْعَصْرُ has the time as its subject, “the ʿaṣr called”; Classical would say أُذِّنَ لِلْعَصْرِ. The ʿaṣr is the mid-afternoon prayer.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجْتُ وَجِئْتُ مَنْزِلِي فَعَبَسَتْ زَوْجَتِي فَقَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-kharajtu wa-jiʾtu manzilī fa-ʿabasat zawjatī fa-qālat
sentences.l: So I-went-out and came (to) my-house; so my-wife frowned, and she-said:
sentences.i: I went out and came to my house, and my wife scowled and said:

sentences.t: أَنْتَ فِي حَظِّكَ وَأُنْسِكَ وَأَنَا مَحْزُونَةٌ
sentences.tr: anta fī ḥaẓẓika wa-unsika wa-anā maḥzūnatun
sentences.l: You (are) in your-luck and your-pleasant-company, and I (am) grieved.
sentences.i: You are in your good fortune and your pleasant company, and I am left to grieve.

sentences.t: أَنْ لَمْ تُخْرِجْنِي وَتُفَرِّجْنِي بَقِيَّةَ النَّهَارِ قَطَعْتُ حَبْلِي وَيَصِيرُ سَبَبَ فِرَاقِي مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: an lam tukhrijnī wa-tufarrijnī baqiyyata al-nahāri qaṭaʿtu ḥablī wa-yaṣīru sababa firāqī minka
sentences.l: If you-do-not take-me-out and make-me-stroll (for) the-rest (of) the-day, I-have-cut my-rope, and it-becomes (the) cause (of) my-parting from-you.
sentences.i: If you do not take me out and give me a stroll for the rest of the day, I shall cut my rope, and that will be the cause of my parting from you.
sentences.n: The print has أن where Classical has إِنْ, “if”; we vocalise it as the conditional. “To cut one’s rope” is to sever the tie, and the perfect قَطَعْتُ in the main clause makes the threat sound already done.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُهَا وَخَرَجْتُ بِهَا وَتَفَرَّجْنَا إِلَى الْعِشَاءِ ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا فَلَقِينَا هَذَا الْأَحْدَبَ وَالسُّكْرُ طَافِحٌ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ يُنْشِدُ هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtuhā wa-kharajtu bihā wa-tafarrajnā ilā al-ʿishāʾi thumma rajaʿnā fa-laqīnā hādhā al-aḥdaba wa-al-sukru ṭāfiḥun minhu wa-huwa yunshidu hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: So I-took her and went-out with-her, and we-strolled until the-evening, then we-returned and met this the-hunchback, and the-drunkenness (was) brimming from-him, and he (was) reciting these two the-verses.
sentences.i: So I took her and went out with her, and we strolled until evening; then we turned back and met this hunchback, brimming over with drink, reciting these two verses:

sentences.t:
رَقَّ الزُّجَاجُ وَرَقَّتِ الْخَمْرُ * فَتَشَابَهَا فَتَشَاكَلَ الْاَمْرُ
فَكَاَنَّمَا خَمْرٌ وَلَا قَدَحٌ * وَكَاَنَّمَا قَدَحٌ وَلَا خَمْرُ
sentences.tr:
raqqa al-zujāju wa-raqqati al-khamru * fa-tashābahā fa-tashākala al-amru
fa-ka-annamā khamrun wa-lā qadaḥun * wa-ka-annamā qadaḥun wa-lā khamru
sentences.l:
Grew-fine the-glass and grew-fine the-wine * so the-two resembled-each-other, so became-alike the-matter,
so as-though (it were) wine and no cup * and as-though (it were) cup and no wine.
sentences.i:
The glass grew fine, and the wine grew fine, * the two grew alike, and the matter was confused:
it seems all wine and no cup, * and then all cup and no wine.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print. The glass and the wine are so clear and delicate that they cannot be told apart. تَشَابَهَا is a dual verb, “the two resembled each other”.

sentences.t: فَعَزَمْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَخَرَجْتُ أَشْتَرِي سَمَكًا مَقْلِيًّا وَجَلَسْنَا نَأْكُلُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿazamtu ʿalayhi wa-kharajtu ashtarī samakan maqliyyan wa-jalasnā naʾkulu
sentences.l: So I-pressed upon-him (to join us), and went-out buying fish fried, and we-sat eating.
sentences.i: I pressed him to join us, and went out to buy fried fish, and we sat down to eat.
sentences.n: عَزَمَ عَلَى: “to press someone (to accept an invitation)”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ زَوْجَتِي أَعْطَتْهُ لُقْمَةً وَقِطْعَةَ سَمَكٍ وَأَدْخَلَتْهُمَا فَمَهُ وَسَدَّتْهُ فَمَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna zawjatī aʿṭathu luqmatan wa-qiṭʿata samakin wa-adkhalathumā famahu wa-saddathu fa-māta
sentences.l: Then indeed my-wife gave-him a-morsel and a-piece (of) fish, and put-them-both (into) his-mouth and stopped-it up, and he-died.
sentences.i: Then my wife handed him a morsel and a piece of fish, thrust both into his mouth and stopped it, and he died.
sentences.n: فَمَهُ is the Middle Arabic form of the accusative “his mouth”; Classical has فَاهُ.

sentences.t: فَحَمَلْتُهُ وَتَحَايَلْتُ وَرَمَيْتُهُ فِي بَيْتِ هَذَا الطَّبِيبِ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَتَحَايَلَ الطَّبِيبُ وَرَمَاهُ فِي بَيْتِ الشَّاهِدِ وَتَحَايَلَ الشَّاهِدُ وَرَمَاهُ فِي طَرِيقِ النَّصْرَانِيِّ السِّمْسَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamaltuhu wa-taḥāyaltu wa-ramaytuhu fī bayti hādhā al-ṭabībi al-yahūdiyyi wa-taḥāyala al-ṭabību wa-ramāhu fī bayti al-shāhidi wa-taḥāyala al-shāhidu wa-ramāhu fī ṭarīqi al-naṣrāniyyi al-simsāri
sentences.l: So I-carried-him and schemed and threw-him in the-house (of) this the-physician the-Jewish; and the-physician schemed and threw-him in the-house (of) the-witness; and the-witness schemed and threw-him in the-road (of) the-Christian the-broker.
sentences.i: So I carried him off and, by a stratagem, threw him into the house of this Jewish physician; and the physician contrived to throw him into the house of the witness; and the witness contrived to throw him into the path of the Christian broker.
sentences.n: تَحَايَلَ is “to resort to a ruse”. الشَّاهِد here is the legal witness who attests contracts.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ قِصَّتِي وَمَا لَا قَيْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ فَمَا هِيَ بِأَ عْجَبَ مِنْ قِصَّةِ الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi qiṣṣatī wa-mā lāqaytu al-bāriḥata fa-mā hiya bi-aʿjaba min qiṣṣati al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: And this (is) my-story and what I-met last-night; and it-is-not more-wondrous than the-story (of) the-hunchback.
sentences.i: This is my story, and what befell me last night; and it is no stranger than the hunchback’s tale.
sentences.n: The print breaks two words with a space: لا قيت for لاقيت (“I met with”) and با عجب for بأعجب (“more wondrous”). The بِـ after مَا only marks the negated predicate; the comparative أَعْجَبُ is followed by مِنْ, “than”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ مَلِكُ الصِّينِ هَذِهِ الْقِصَّةَ هَزَّ رَأْسَهُ طَرَبًا وَأَبْدَى عَجَبًا وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa maliku al-ṣīni hādhihi al-qiṣṣata hazza raʾsahu ṭaraban wa-abdā ʿajaban wa-qāla
sentences.l: So when the-king (of) China heard this the-story, he-shook his-head (in) delight, and showed wonder, and said:
sentences.i: When the King of China heard this tale, he shook his head in delight, showed his wonder, and said:

sentences.t: هَذِهِ الْقِصَّةُ الَّتِي جَرَتْ بَيْنَ هَذَا الشَّابِّ وَالْمُزَيِّنِ الْفُضُولِيِّ إِنَّهَا لَأَطْرَبُ وَأَحْسَنُ مِنْ قِصَّةِ الْأَحْدَبِ الْأَكْذَبِ
sentences.tr: hādhihi al-qiṣṣatu allatī jarat bayna hādhā al-shābbi wa-al-muzayyini al-fuḍūliyyi innahā la-aṭrabu wa-aḥsanu min qiṣṣati al-aḥdabi al-akdhabi
sentences.l: This the-story that happened between this the-youth and the-barber the-meddlesome, indeed-it (is) surely more-delightful and better than the-story (of) the-hunchback the-falsest.
sentences.i: This tale that passed between the young man and the meddlesome barber is surely more delightful and better than the tale of that hunchback, that arch-liar.
sentences.n: The sentence opens with the topic (“this tale…”) and picks it up with إِنَّهَا, “indeed it…”. الْأَكْذَب, “the falsest”, is obscure here; it may be a loose intensifier of الأحدب (“the lying hunchback”), and we read it so.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَمَرَ بَعْضَ حُجَّابِهِ أَنِ امْضُوا مَعَ الْخَيَّاطِ وَ أَحْضِرُوا الْمُزَيِّنَ مِنَ الْحَبْسِ وَأَسْمَعَ كَلَامَهُ وَيَكُونَ سَبَبَ خَلَاصِكُمْ أَنْتُمُ الْجَمِيعُ وَنَدْفِنَ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika amara baʿḍa ḥujjābihi ani imḍū maʿa al-khayyāṭi wa-aḥḍirū al-muzayyina min al-ḥabsi wa-asmaʿa kalāmahu wa-yakūna sababa khalāṣikum antum al-jamīʿu wa-nadfina hādhā al-aḥdaba
sentences.l: Then indeed the-king commanded some (of) his-chamberlains: that go with the-tailor, and bring the-barber from the-prison, and (that) I-hear his-speech, and (that) be (the) cause (of) your-deliverance, you, the-all, and (that) we-bury this the-hunchback.
sentences.i: Then the king commanded some of his chamberlains: “Go with the tailor and bring the barber out of the prison, that I may hear his speech; it shall be the cause of your deliverance, all of you, and then we shall bury this hunchback.”
sentences.n: The command begins with أَنِ and plain imperatives, then slips into the king’s own purpose (“that I may hear”). We vocalise the later verbs as subjunctives, continuing أَنْ. The print leaves a stray space after the first و.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And overtook Shahrazād the-morning, so she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula of the night, in rhymed prose: ṣabāḥ / mubāḥ. “The permitted speech” is the tale she is allowed to tell.
